Three callers fetch rows by index inside a loop: `CSSRTradingEngine::RestoreFrom` for `pos` (`Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1172-1177`) and for `leg` (`:1225-1231`), and `CSSRStatsEngine::RestoreFrom` for every equity sample (`Trading/SSR_Statistics.mqh:645-651`). The class's own comment (`:45-47`) justifies the linear scan because "sessions are small enough", which holds for a scalar `Get` and not for these three loops. `Restore` runs on the host's `OnInit` path (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1483`) with the terminal blocked. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Corrected arithmetic: the reachable worst case is ~8,760 entries (not 12,800), giving roughly 512×8,760 + 4,096×8,760 + 4,096×8,760 ≈ **76 million key comparisons**; a typical session of tens of trades and hundreds of samples is three to four orders of magnitude cheaper.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** The operation count follows from the code; the **wall time** does not — MQL5 string-comparison cost is a runtime property, and nothing in the tree measures it.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Write a synthetic worst-case session file (512 `pos` rows, 8 `leg` rows each, 4,096 `e` rows) with a script, then wrap `CSSRSessionManager::Restore` in `GetMicrosecondCount()` and resume it. Record the elapsed milliseconds. **Confirms as a defect** if it exceeds ~500 ms (a visible freeze at startup); **clears** if it is under ~50 ms. Repeat with a realistic 60-trade session to see the normal case. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Index entries by section on load — one pass, one array of first-index-per-section — which turns all three loops linear.

#### D.1.20 `ui-port-session-15` — LOW — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Common/SSR_SessionFile.mqh:212`
*The session file is written in the terminal's ANSI codepage.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Both ends use `FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI` — write at `:138`, read at `:212` — i.e. one byte per character through the machine's ANSI codepage. The exposed user text is the position **tag**: typed into the panel's tagbox `OBJ_EDIT`, read by `CSSRPanel::ReadTag` (`Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:2537-2559`), passed through `CSSRGroupPort::SetTradeTag`, which only trims and strips commas (`Ui/SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-809`), packed into the `pos` row (`Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1105`) and read back at `:1209` with no validation — plus the session **name** and **bookmark labels** written in the same mode (`Core/SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1752`). **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** One correction: `note` is a dormant field — a grep finds no producer anywhere, only the read-back at `:1210` — so there is one user-authored string at risk, not two. The project has already recorded this exact lesson for the *read* direction: `fa.txt` is read `FILE_BIN` + `CharArrayToString(..., CP_UTF8)` with an explicit BOM skip (`Ui/SSR_Strings.mqh:663-686`), precisely because `FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI` hands back one character per byte.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether the round trip is lossy (`?` substitution) or merely machine-dependent (CP1256 bytes that are mojibake on a Western install) depends on the terminal's ANSI codepage.

**Exact real-terminal test.** On a Persian-locale Windows: open a trade, tag it with a Persian word, save the session, resume it, and read the tag off the panel and out of the statement. Then copy the same `.ssr` file to a machine with a Western ANSI codepage and resume it there. **Confirms** if either read-back differs from what was typed. Inspect the file's bytes with a hex viewer to distinguish the two failure modes. A mangled tag loses an annotation only — no trade figure is affected, which is why this stays LOW.

#### D.1.21 `trading-analytics-13` — LOW — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_Journal.mqh:254`
*Exports written `FILE_ANSI` while the statement declares UTF-8.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Both exports open `FILE_WRITE | FILE_TXT | FILE_ANSI` — CSV at `:173`, HTML at `:254` — while the HTML head hard-codes `<meta charset="utf-8">` (`Report/SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:21`), and there is no `CP_UTF8` conversion or `FileWriteArray` path anywhere in the file. The session name is user text (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1355`, `SetSession(CfgSession(), ...)` from the setup panel's edit box), as are tags, and both are printed into the CSV header (`:190`) and the HTML (`:269`). The product ships a complete Persian translation.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Every literal the journal itself writes is ASCII, so the defect needs a Persian session name or tag, and the byte-level outcome — `?` substitution versus CP1256 bytes rendered as mojibake by a UTF-8-declaring browser — is a property of the terminal's ANSI codepage.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Name a session in Persian, take one trade, export both the CSV and the HTML statement. Open the HTML in a browser (it declares UTF-8) and the CSV in Excel. **Confirms** if the name renders as `?????` or as mojibake in either. Hex-dump the file to see which. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Write both files with `FILE_BIN` + `StringToCharArray(..., CP_UTF8)` and emit a BOM, mirroring the proven read path in `SSR_Strings.mqh`.

#### D.1.22 `trading-analytics-14` — LOW — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_Journal.mqh:51`
*CSV escaping does not handle the double quote.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `Csv()` (`:51-58`) replaces `,` with `;` and CR/LF with a space, and never doubles or wraps a double quote; it is the only sanitiser applied to `m_sess_name`, `m_sess_seed`, `SessionKey()`, `st.Caveat()`, `p.tag` and `p.note`. `SetTradeTag` strips commas only (`Ui/SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-809`), and `InpSession` is a raw MQL5 input string, so a `"` can reach the file — the tag lands at column 3 (`:75`) and the session name in the `# session` header (`:190`). **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** One correction: only a field whose **first** character is a quote triggers RFC-4180 quoted-field parsing; the original "12&quot; chart" example (quote mid-field) is parsed literally by both Excel and pandas and merges nothing. The project's own reader is unaffected — `SSR_ClassReport.mqh`'s `Split()` is comma-only.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether a given reader actually swallows delimiters and line breaks is a property of that third-party reader, not of this code, and no live path sets a leading quote today.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Tag one trade with `"scalp` (leading double quote) and name the session `"test`. Export the CSV and open it in Excel, then in `pandas.read_csv`. **Confirms** if rows shift or merge in either. **[RECOMMENDATION]** In `Csv()`, if the field contains `"`, double every quote and wrap the field — three lines, and the question is closed for every reader.

#### D.1.23 `ui-dialogs-8` — LOW — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:289`
*`Num()` turns a thousands separator into a decimal point.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `StringReplace(t, ",", ".")` at `:289` is unconditional and runs before `StringToDouble`, so `"10,000"` is parsed as the well-formed literal `"10.000"` = 10.0 and passes both the unreadable-guard at `:295` (`v != 0.0`) and `ReadAll`'s `<= 0.0` clamp at `:1191`. The comma replacement exists deliberately, because the field is meant to accept comma decimals. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** The original claim's load-bearing half is refuted, which is why this is LOW and a UX issue rather than a silent 1000x misconfiguration: step 3's `RenderStart` recaps the parsed value — `Recap("bal2", "Balance", DoubleToString(m_v.balance, 2))` at `:879` — and `go` exists only on that same step (`:940`), so a balance of 10.00 is displayed above the START button on every path that can have typed it. The quick paths (`qlast`/`qcont`/`qrand`) have no Balance box at all.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** The `"1,234.56" → 1.234` half rests on `StringToDouble`'s prefix-parse behaviour for a malformed double-dot string, which MQL5 does not document — and if it returned `0.0` the `:295` guard would restore the fallback, which is *safer*, not worse.

**Exact real-terminal test.** In the setup wizard, type `10,000` in Balance and step through to START: read the Balance recap. Then type `1,234.56` and do the same. **Confirms the ambiguity** if the recaps read `10.00` and `1.23`. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Reject any string containing more than one separator and show the parsed value inline in the field's own row, rather than only two steps later.

#### D.1.24 `ui-plumbing-13` — LOW — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Strings.mqh:472`
*Raw UTF-8 bytes in drawn literals with no BOM.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** A byte scan of all 123 `.mqh`/`.mq5` files found exactly two non-ASCII sources and neither carries a UTF-8 BOM: `SSR_Strings.mqh` (18 non-ASCII bytes — six U+00B7 at `:472` ×2, `:474` ×1 and `:544` ×3, inside the drawn literals `SSR_S_PAL_HINT`, `SSR_S_PAL_OF` and `SSR_S_SU_SUMMARY`, plus three Persian characters in a comment at `:651`) and `Ui/SSR_ReviewCard.mqh:155` (`pre = "· "`, 2 bytes). All 121 other files are pure ASCII. If MetaEditor decodes a BOM-less source as the system ANSI code page rather than UTF-8, each `C2 B7` becomes two characters and the palette footer draws `Enter runs  Â·  Up / Down chooses`. The compile succeeds either way, so nothing in the build reports it.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** How MetaEditor resolves the encoding of a file it was given no mark for is terminal/OS-locale behaviour.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Compile the project in MetaEditor on a Windows install whose system locale is **not** UTF-8 (a Persian or Russian ANSI codepage is the sharpest case), start the EA and press Ctrl+K. **Confirms** if the palette footer or the setup summary shows `Â·` instead of `·`. **[RECOMMENDATION]** The fix does not need the answer, because the runtime path is already proven safe (`fa.txt` is read `FILE_BIN` + `CP_UTF8` and carries the same U+00B7 correctly): replace the six literals with an ASCII separator and the project keeps all-ASCII sources. Worst case if left alone is cosmetic — no control flow, key handling or 63-character budget depends on it.

#### D.1.25 `qa-smoke-6` — LOW — `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/QA/SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:359`
*The opening leftover sweep can close the chart the script itself runs on.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** The sweep (`:352-364`, tail built at `:350` from `SSR_SYMBOL_SUFFIX + InpSlot`) walks `ChartFirst`/`ChartNext` and closes every chart whose symbol ends in that tail, with **no `id == ChartID()` exclusion**. Dropped on a chart of `<origin>.SSR9` with `InpSlot=9`, it closes its own chart three log lines in; `qa-result.txt` then holds three lines and stops and the `Comment` vanishes with the chart — indistinguishable from the freeze the file spends sixty lines of comments (`:121-196`, `:265-279`) building instrumentation for. The sweep's own comment (`:344-347`) argues the danger away on the basis of the default slot, but the slot is an input. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Two corrections: `Cleanup()` at `:5466-5475` cannot self-close independently (any chart it would match was already matched and closed by the opening sweep), and the stated side effects are softer than claimed — `Log()` flushes per line (`:222`) and MQL5 closes handles on unload.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether MetaTrader terminates a script when the chart it runs on is closed by that same script is runtime behaviour, and it also needs a user to drop the suite on a replay chart.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Open a chart of `EURUSD.SSR9`, drop `SSR_QA_Smoke` on it with `InpSlot=9`. **Confirms** if the chart closes and `qa-result.txt` stops after the sweep lines. **[RECOMMENDATION]** One `if(id == ChartID()) { id = nxt; continue; }` in the sweep is the whole fix; it is cheaper than the test.

#### D.1.26 `spikes-audits-24` — LOW — `MQL5/Indicators/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_Probe_TickWitness.mq5:56`
*The witness assertion can pass without a single injected tick.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `g_calls++` is the unconditional first statement of `OnCalculate` (`:66`), so it counts every recalculation cause, and the sole verdict is `SSR_Verdict("chart_received_ticks", g_calls > 1, ...)` at `:56`. The counter that actually tests the hypothesis the header states — `g_ticks`, incremented at `:72` only when `close[rates_total-1]` moves — is emitted as a *metric* at `:51` and appears in **no** verdict. `Report()` runs from `OnDeinit`, which for an indicator also fires on timeframe change and recompile, appending a fresh verdict row each time. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** One correction: `ChartRedraw`/chart refresh is **not** among the triggers of `OnCalculate`; the plausible ones are the initial calculation plus a history/rates update (a sibling spike's `CustomRatesUpdate`) or a re-init.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether `g_calls > 1` is reachable with zero injected ticks is MQL5 runtime behaviour. Impact is limited because B1 carries its own `reflect_iclose == nbars` verdict, so the probe is not the only evidence.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Attach `SSR_Probe_TickWitness` to a chart of a custom symbol and inject **nothing**. Wait 60 s, remove it, and read the verdict file. **Confirms** if `chart_received_ticks` comes back PASS. Second variant: attach it, then run any spike that calls `CustomRatesUpdate` on that symbol without adding ticks — **confirms** the same way with a clearer cause. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Assert `g_ticks > 0`, which is the quantity the header says the probe exists to witness.

#### D.1.27 `spikes-audits-31` — LOW — `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_B2_TickThroughput.mq5:172`
*B2 recommends a batch size without measuring how long one call blocks.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `total_us` only accumulates across rounds (`:132`); `inject_time`, `ticks_per_sec` and `us_per_tick` all derive from that sum (`:138-148`); no max or percentile of a single `CustomTicksAdd` is recorded (contrast B1, which does emit per-call `ticksadd_elapsed`). `best_rate`/`best_batch` are selected from the aggregate rate alone (`:156-160`) and published as "lock this into Feeder" (`:172-174`). The quantity the engine actually budgets is **one pump beat** — `InpPumpMs`, default 40 ms (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:78`, `EventSetMillisecondTimer` at `:1574`) — and nothing joins B2's numbers to the jitter probe its own header (`:10-12`) declares mandatory ("Throughput without a responsiveness number is meaningless"); `:190` leaves the join to a human. The header's promise to show throughput collapsing "as charts and indicators are added" is also unimplemented: only `InpCharts` varies, no indicator is ever attached, and `InpLabel` is hand-typed, so a mislabelled run is recorded under the wrong condition. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Two corrections: the *mean* per-call time is recoverable (`inject_time / rounds`), so only the max/p95 tail is unmeasured; and `SSR_Rate` returns -1 unless `accepted == sent` (`SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:365-372`), so partially accepted batches cannot win.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** The empirical prediction that the largest fully-accepted batch necessarily wins the aggregate-rate comparison is an expectation about MetaTrader's per-call cost curve, not something the file proves.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Patch B2 to record `GetMicrosecondCount()` around **each** `CustomTicksAdd`, keep the max and the p95 per case, and run the full batch ladder with `SSR_Probe_UIJitter` attached to a second chart. **Confirms the methodology gap** if the winning batch's max single-call time exceeds 40 ms, or if `ui_jitter_p95` degrades at the winning size. The published recommendation should then be the largest batch whose **p95 single-call time** is under one pump beat, not the best aggregate rate.

#### D.1.28 `tests-a-10` — LOW — `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5:186`
*`SERIES_BARS_COUNT` read after a fixed 900 ms wait, and audit A21 cannot see the line.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** The A21 blind spot is provable: the audit's regex (`tools/ssr_audit.py:1585-1590`) requires the timeframe argument to match `([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\s*\(\s*\))?)` immediately followed by `\s*,\s*SERIES_BARS_COUNT`, and `cycle[i], SERIES_BARS_COUNT` cannot match — the line is in scope (`sources()` walks every `.mq5`) and simply never reported. T3 wrote the retry helper for exactly this hazard — `long SeriesBars(...)` re-reads up to 10 times with `CopyRates` + `Sleep(100)` (`Tests/SSR_T3_CustomSymbol.mq5:48-63`), under a header noting that `SERIES_BARS_COUNT` "answers zero — not 'no bars' but 'no series yet'" — and T4 does not use it. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** One correction: the timeframe is not "unprimed" in the T3.6 sense, because `:171` calls `ChartSetSymbolPeriod(cid, rsym, cycle[i])` on an open chart and a displayed timeframe is itself what touches the series into existence. The real defect is a **fixed `SSRPause(900)` with no re-read**, i.e. a timing race, and exposure is narrower than claimed: only iteration 0 (M15) is at risk, since `FutureBars` at `:190` copies M1/M5/M15/M30/H1/H4 and primes every later iteration. The failure mode is a false FAIL, never a false PASS.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether 900 ms is enough for MetaTrader to build an M15 series on a freshly switched chart depends on the machine and the amount of M1 history.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Restart the terminal (cold caches), run T4 immediately, and record whether T4.2 reports "M15 has bars 0"; repeat ten times, and ten more times with the terminal warm. **Confirms** if any cold run reports 0 while an immediate re-run reports a positive count. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Import T3's `SeriesBars()` retry helper, and widen A21's regex to accept an indexed timeframe argument so the audit can see this class of line at all (this is the only known A21 blind spot; the four CONFIRMED LOW findings against the audit tool itself — `spikes-audits-26`, `-27`, `-28`, `-29` — are in section C and cover its siblings). **There is no finding id `audit-coverage`; an earlier draft of this line used that name and no such id exists in `verified.json`.**

#### D.1.29 `ui-port-session-14` — IMPROVEMENT — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Common/SSR_SessionFile.mqh:33`
*The entry ceiling is enforced on read and not on write.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `Create`/`Section`/`Set` write straight to the handle with no counter and no ceiling test (`:134-192`), while `Load` aborts the **whole file** the moment `m_ent_count >= SSR_SF_MAX_ENTRIES` and returns false (`:251-252`, `:261-269`, with the comment "it was NOT fully read"). So a file above the ceiling can be written, `Save()` returns true, and it is then permanently unopenable. The comment at `:30-32` that justifies the ceiling counts "4096 equity samples + 512 positions + four streams of settings" and omits the **leg** rows entirely. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Corrected arithmetic, since the original finding's own numbers were wrong: worst case is 4,096 `e` rows (`SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES`, `Trading/SSR_Statistics.mqh:33`) + 512 `pos` + 512×8 = 4,096 `leg` rows (`SSR_MAX_POSITIONS` = 512, `SSR_MAX_TRADE_LEGS` = 8) + ~20 keys and ≤16 bookmarks per stream ≈ **8,760 entries, about 53% of 16,384** — headroom of ~1.9x, not the comment's claimed 3x, and not the 78% the finding stated.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Unreachable at today's constants. It becomes live the moment someone raises `SSR_MAX_POSITIONS` or `SSR_EQUITY_SAMPLES` **on the strength of that comment** — then saves keep reporting success and every one of them is unopenable.

**Exact real-terminal test.** Write a synthetic `.ssr` with 17,000 entries (a script looping `Set`) and attempt to load it through `CSSRSessionManager`. **Confirms** if `Save` reports success and `Load` returns false with no repair path. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Count entries on write, fail `Save()` at the ceiling with a message naming the limit, and correct the headroom comment to ~1.9x.

#### D.1.30 `trading-analytics-15` — IMPROVEMENT — `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Trading/SSR_ShotBook.mqh:164`
*Screenshots are taken on the chart the control panel is drawn on.*

**The claim.** **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** `ChartScreenShot` targets `m_chart`, set from `g_replay_chart` (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1281`, `:2655`), and nothing in `Shoot()`/`Flush()` (`:150-173`) hides, moves or restores panel objects. In the default configuration (`InpOneChart=true`, `:131`) the second pass makes the EA's own chart the replay chart (`g_replay_chart = ChartID()`, `:1276`) while the panel is created on that same chart (`g_panel_chart = ChartID()`, `:1463`), so the panel and any open card are inside every entry/exit PNG, and `ALIGN_RIGHT` anchors the capture on the latest bars — the region the panel may cover. `InpShots` defaults to true (`:144`). **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Narrower than first stated: with `InpOneChart=false` the replay chart is a separate window carrying no panel, so those PNGs are clean.

**Why it could not be settled from source.** Whether the panel actually occludes the traded bars depends on the runtime panel corner (`SetCorner`/`SnapToCorner`) and the chart geometry, and `ChartScreenShot` output on a chart this program is not attached to is unvalidated.

**Exact real-terminal test.** One-window mode, panel in its default corner, take one trade and open the produced PNG from `MQL5\Files`. **Confirms** if the panel covers the entry bar or the right-hand price action. Repeat with the panel moved to each of the four corners (Ctrl+K → "Move the panel to the next corner") to find the corner that is clean. **[RECOMMENDATION]** Hide the panel's objects for the duration of the capture (`OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES = OBJ_NO_PERIODS` on the widget prefix, screenshot, restore) — the widget layer already has `Hide()` for exactly this — or, better, keep `InpOneChart=false` for anyone who relies on screenshots.

---

### Refuted

**21 findings.** These were raised by the subsystem readers, put to the same three adversarial refuters as everything else, and **did not survive**. They are printed because the refutations are the audit's quality control: they show what was examined, what the guard was, and where a plausible-looking reading of the source was wrong. **None of these may be presented as a defect.** Where a refutation left a residue worth doing something about, it is marked **[RECOMMENDATION]** and carries no severity.

Refutation classes: **9 unreachable state** · **6 a guard exists one layer up** · **4 MQL5 or design semantics misread** · **2 documented intent**.

| id | file:line | what was claimed | why it was refuted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chart-16` | `Chart/SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:83` | Index-named news objects would pin a stale event if the calendar were redrawn after a reload | **Unreachable.** `Draw()` has one caller (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:940`), reached once per program instance from `BuildSession`; `g_cal.Load` never re-runs, `OnRewind` only resets announce flags, and `Clear()` wipes the prefix on every deinit (`:2120`). **[RECOMMENDATION]** name objects by event, not index, before anyone adds a reload |
| `chart-15` | `Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:596` | `SetPeriodAll` would restart the EA mid-loop in one-chart mode | **Unreachable + semantics misread.** Grep finds no caller anywhere; and `ChartSetSymbolPeriod` is asynchronous (the codebase says so at `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2186`), so the loop and the trailing `Sync()` would complete before any reinit. **[RECOMMENDATION]** add the `id == ChartID()` skip `CloseOwned` already has |
| `chart-9` | `Chart/SSR_LeakGuard.mqh:59` | A live correlated chart is counted then discarded, so the panel says "no leak" | **Design intent.** `IsClean()` deliberately scopes a leak to the **origin** symbol; the scan cannot tell a correlated instrument from any unrelated chart the user has open, so folding `other_live_charts` in would fire on nearly every desktop. Residue is a dead field and an unassigned enum value |
| `core-sync-5` | `Core/Sources/SSR_MemoryDataSource.mqh:270` | `Ticks()` returning NULL leaves the tick provider unguarded and can dangle a freed guard | **Unreachable.** `CSSRMemoryDataSource::LoadTicks` has **no caller** in the tree, so the store never holds ticks, `Ticks()` is always NULL and FULL_TICK always degrades; guard layer 1 in `EmitWindow` clamps before every read regardless. **[RECOMMENDATION]** override `SetGuard`/`DetachGuard` as `CSSRMt5DataSource` does, before anything starts loading ticks |
| `data-6` | `Data/SSR_Calendar.mqh:179` | The calendar draws every future release at session start, showing the trader what is coming | **Documented intent.** `SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:10-14`: "THE FUTURE IS DRAWN ON PURPOSE... a real trader knows the calendar days ahead"; `:16-18` names blind mode as the one exception, which the host enforces at `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:925-929` |
| `data-10` | `Data/SSR_SessionRange.mqh:86` | A range running past the broker's last bar validates clean and replays ten days of nothing | **Guard downstream + unreachable.** `CSSRReplayTimeline::SetWindow` clamps `end_msc` to `data_last_msc` (`SSR_ReplayTimeline.mqh:66-67`) and the controller refuses a collapsed window (`:775-782`); the only production caller seeds `end_msc` from `m_cat.LastMsc()` and edits start alone (`SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:109`, `:272`) |
| `strategy-integration-report-11` | `Integration/SSR_Client.mqh:201` | A co-hosted client's spin-wait starves the EA's `OnTimer`, so every command is refused | **MQL5 semantics misread.** MQL5 does not run every program on a chart in one thread: each EA (and script) has its own; only indicators of one symbol share one, and a second EA cannot be on the same chart. `Poll()` writes the ack from `OnTimer` every `InpPumpMs` (40 ms), well inside the 500 ms timeout. Residue is the documented cost at `:211-212`: a burned core, and an occupied indicator thread |
| `strategy-integration-report-14` | `Report/SSR_ClassReport.mqh:356` | `Html()` escapes four of the five characters its comment names, and `SSRWriteReportHead` interpolates its title unescaped | **No reachable path.** Every attribute the writer emits is double-quoted; each `Html()` sink (`:521, 561, 618, 650, 652`) is element text content, where an apostrophe needs no escaping; the one interpolated attribute is fed `SSRFormatMsc` (digits, dots, colons); both `SSRWriteReportHead` call sites pass literals. **[RECOMMENDATION]** add `&#39;` and escape the title anyway — two lines |
| `ui-port-session-6` | `Session/SSR_SessionManager.mqh:197` | The prop evaluation is not persisted, so a resumed challenge restarts silently while the panel presents it as authoritative | **Guard exists.** `Restore` ends in `NotifyRestored()` → `PublishRewind(now)` → `CSSRPropEvaluation::OnRewind`, which sets `SSR_PROP_VOID` with a reason (`SSR_PropEvaluation.mqh:440-452`); the headline then reads "VOID — ..." and the host prints "a rewind voids the run — that is deliberate" at init. The evaluation is also opt-in (`CfgProp()`). Residue: a run saved as PASSED/FAILED comes back RUNNING after `Reset()` — filed separately as `trading-analytics-2` |
| `ui-port-session-5` | `Session/SSR_SessionManager.mqh:334` | The wind-forward re-emits the crossed stretch into a still-live account | **Guards + scope.** `JumpForward` writes the bulk straight to the sink with `SeedBars` and publishes nothing to observers (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1378-1389`); only the target's own M1 bar goes through `EmitWindow`, and the account is then overwritten wholesale by `RestoreFrom`. Auto-pause, shot book and prop are all reset by `NotifyRestored`. Residue: the comment at `:332-333` is stale |

What remains is an absent broker-convention refinement in an explicitly declared simplification |

| `ui-plumbing-7` | `Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:135` | `Mix()` is a mod-2^64 polynomial hash, so the cache's "NO HASH, AND THEREFORE NO COLLISION" is false and a widget can keep a stale colour | **No reachable collision.** The arithmetic is right, but every colour argument is a compile-time palette token (A17 enforces it): brute force over all three palettes (51 + 51 + 35 tokens) finds **no** pair `(bg+d, edge-d*1000003)` with `abs(d) <= 16`, and overflow collisions need a full 64-bit cancellation. Residue is a falsified comment, not a wrong pixel |

Residue: a stale comment |

Asserting a collaborator's contract at the seam is defence in depth |

### Coverage statement

Silence is ambiguous in an audit: a subsystem with no finding may have been clean, or may not have been read. This subsection removes the ambiguity for every area that produced **no defect**. Each line names the files and states the checks that were run against them. **No bug has been invented to fill a line** — where an area is not clean, it is said so explicitly rather than omitted.

**Scope of the read.** 123 `.mq5`/`.mqh` files, 51,278 lines, read in full by seventeen subsystem agents. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] 90 of the 123 carry at least one finding; 33 carry none — 90 + 33 = 123.** `verified.json` holds **91** distinct `file` values, one more than 90, because the ninety-first is `tools/ssr_audit.py`, which is a Python tool and not one of the 123 MQL files. It carries **four** findings — `spikes-audits-26`, `-27`, `-28` and `-29`, all CONFIRMED, all LOW. All 33 files that carry **no** `verified.json` entry are enumerated below with the area they belong to, and the enumeration has been recomputed against `verified.json`: every one of the 33 is named. Of those 33, **two are named as explicitly NOT clean** even though `verified.json` holds no finding against them — `Trading/SSR_RiskEngine.mqh` (section H reads nine defects from it and its immediate callers, registered `new-7` … `new-15` in D.2) and `Services/SSReplay/Spike/SSR_C1_ServiceApiAccess.mq5` (one of the two call sites named by `spikes-audits-16`) — and **one is clean with a stated qualification**, `Common/SSR_Random.mqh` (no finding survived; section J records two non-defect observations in it). **So: 31 of the 33 are enumerated as clean, and the two exceptions are named rather than omitted.** The remaining coverage lines are hazard classes checked across the whole tree.

#### Hazard classes checked tree-wide

- **Checked — no defect found in any of the 123 files: no real-order path exists.** `OrderSend`, `OrderSendAsync`, `CTrade` and `PositionClose` appear 7 times across `MQL5/` and **every occurrence is a comment asserting their absence** (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:305`, `Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:6`, `Trading/SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:5`, `Strategy/SSR_IStrategy.mqh:8` and `:18`, `Integration/SSR_Publisher.mqh:19`, `Ui/SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:341`). All trading is virtual; no finding in this audit describes a path to a broker. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**
- **Checked — no defect found in the 121 files outside `Ui/SSR_Strings.mqh` and `Ui/SSR_ReviewCard.mqh`: source encoding.** Every file was byte-scanned; only those two carry non-ASCII bytes, and both are covered by `ui-plumbing-13` (D.1.24). No other drawn literal, comment or identifier depends on how MetaEditor resolves an encoding. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**
- **Checked — no defect found in swap modelling: `Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:388-430` (`AccrueSwap`).** The only candidate raised (`trading-exec-14`) was refuted: the accrual is per crossed midnight of the **server** tick clock, as its header declares. The missing rollover hour and triple-swap day are an acknowledged modelling gap, not a fault. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**

- **Checked — no defect found in the object-name space across the nine drawing prefixes.** Every `CSSRWidgets` instance in the product attaches with an **explicit** prefix, so none inherits the constructor default `"SSR_"` (`Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:168`) that would sweep every other family: `SSRX_` (`SSR_Palette.mqh:87`), `SSRF_` (`SSR_FirstRun.mqh:86`), `SSRK_` (`SSR_KeyCard.mqh:71`), `SSRS_` (`SSR_SetupPanel.mqh:486`), `SSRV_` (`SSR_RevealCard.mqh:66`), `SSRR2_` (`SSR_ReviewCard.mqh:84`), plus `SSRP_`, `SSRD_` and `SSRSD_` passed as constructor defaults (`SSR_Panel.mqh:302`, `SSR_RangeDialog.mqh:79`, `SSR_SessionDialog.mqh:63`). The nine are **pairwise non-prefixing**, so no `ObjectsDeleteAll(chart, prefix)` (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:639`) can reach another family's objects — including the un-prefixed chart-side families `SSR_POS_` (`Chart/SSR_TradeLines.mqh:411`), `SSR_HIST_` (`:517`), `SSR_LINE_SL/TP/EN` (`:163-164`), `SSR_MARK_` (`Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:170`), `SSR_NEWS_` (`Chart/SSR_CalendarLines.mqh:30`) and `SSR_PICK_LINE` (`Ui/SSR_Theme.mqh:508`), none of which begins with any widget prefix. Every `RemoveAll()` call site in the ten widget-owning classes either immediately follows its `Attach` or is guarded by the owner's own `m_chart != 0`. A sweep of repeated draw-id literals *within* each prefix returns six in `SSR_Panel.mqh` and twelve in `SSR_SetupPanel.mqh`; every one examined is either an id built by concatenation (`"tab" + IntegerToString(i)`, `:1157`, `:1215`) or the same logical control drawn by two mutually exclusive layout branches (`lines`/`sessions`/`fidelity`/`tabline` at `:1193-1198`, `:1260` for `SSR_LAYOUT_RAIL` against `:1249-1260` for the 420 fallback) or one object hidden and shown (`tagbox`, `:1299`, `:1375-1376`). **The genuine same-name collisions in this product are all *within* one prefix and are all already filed**: `ui-panel-5` (two cache slots write `setuprow`), `chart-17` (bookmark names carry a registry index), `ui-plumbing-6` (no tombstones, so `Keep()` writes a duplicate slot) and `tests-b-15` (the duplicate-name check masked by a timeframe check). **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**
- **Checked — the forced-liquidation loop terminates and its arithmetic is sound: `Trading/SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:436` (`CheckStopout`), called at `:613` on every tick of every batch.** The loop is bounded by `SSR_MAX_POSITIONS` iterations; each iteration either closes exactly one position or returns, so it cannot spin. `used` is recomputed after every close (`:466`) and **every** division by it is short-circuit-guarded by `used <= 0.0` first (`:441`, `:467`), so the changing denominator cannot produce a divide-by-zero. Worst-loser-first whole-position closing is a declared modelling choice, not an omission — the header at `:433-434` states the intent, and partial liquidation is a different broker policy, not a correction to this one. No `verified.json` finding is filed against it and none is invented here. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**
- **One consequence of that loop that no section previously drew.** `CheckStopout` returns immediately when `m_stopout_level <= 0.0 || m_margin_per_lot <= 0.0` (`:438-439`), and **both** feeding inputs default to zero — `InpMarginLot = 0.0` and `InpStopout = 0.0` (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:94-95`, installed at `:1168-1169`). **Stop-out is therefore dead in the shipped configuration.** Section G's G-6 (registered `new-6` in D.2) records that the whole cost model is frictionless at defaults; this is the sharper form of it, and it bounds `trading-exec-6`: the "unaffordable order is booked, charged, then stopped out" scenario **cannot occur at defaults**, because nothing is ever stopped out at defaults. `trading-exec-6` remains CONFIRMED — the missing pre-trade margin gate is real — but its stated consequence needs a non-zero `InpMarginLot` and `InpStopout` to be reached. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]**
- **Checked — a mid-run chart-timeframe change by the user is detected and handled: `Chart/SSR_ChartManager.mqh:384-400`.** The registry sweep compares `ChartPeriod(id)` against the recorded period, and on a change it records the switch (`tf_changes++`), clears the scroll-detach state that no longer describes the view (`user_detached = false`, `detach_votes = 0`, `last_offset = ViewOffset(id)`), re-applies the follow policy when the chart was following, and notifies the observer via `OnTimeframeChanged`. The comment at `:381-383` states the reasoning: MetaTrader rebuilds the series from the same M1 base, so replay state is untouched. No defect is filed against this path and none is invented here. **[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]** Two residues are stated rather than swept: (a) `OnTimeframeChanged` is declared on the observer interface (`Chart/SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:72`) and implemented by **one** caller in the whole tree, the T4 test (`Tests/SSR_T4_ChartIntegration.mq5:52`) — the EA host does not implement it, which is consistent with the manager already doing the catching-up itself, so it is a dormant seam and not a defect; (b) **[POTENTIAL_RISK]** whether the newly selected timeframe's series is already built at the instant of the switch is the same lazy-build question as `qa-smoke-1` (ground truth: the first `Bars()` on an untouched timeframe returns 0), and whether `CHART_SHOW_DATE_SCALE` / `_OHLC` / `_PRICE_SCALE` set by `CSSRBlindMode::Apply` (`Chart/SSR_BlindMode.mqh:168-172`) survive a period switch is a terminal behaviour nobody here has measured. Both are runtime questions, routed to section U's **U-31B** rather than filed as findings.
- **Checked — the product's key bindings against MetaTrader's own chart keys: stated as an open question, not as a clean result. [POTENTIAL_RISK]** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The bindings are a flat table of 22 distinct virtual-key codes in `Ui/SSR_Keys.mqh:46-75`, and ten of them are keys MetaTrader itself binds on a chart: `SSR_VK_LEFT` 37, `SSR_VK_RIGHT` 39, `SSR_VK_UP` 38, `SSR_VK_DOWN` 40 (chart scroll), `SSR_VK_PGUP` 33, `SSR_VK_PGDN` 34 (chart paging), `SSR_VK_PLUS` 187 / `SSR_VK_NUMPLUS` 107 and `SSR_VK_MINUS` 189 / `SSR_VK_NUMMIN` 109 (chart zoom). They reach the product only through `CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN` on **the chart the EA is attached to** (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3217`, `:3232`), and the panel is created on that same chart (`g_panel_chart = ChartID()`, `:1463`) — the host itself distinguishes the case where it is also the replay chart from the case where it is not (`:1669`). **What is unknown from source:** whether the terminal acts on those ten keys *in addition to* delivering them, and which window has focus when a user is watching the replay chart in a two-window bench. `ui-plumbing-2`, `-3`, `-14` and `-15` cover the conflict class *internal* to the product (wrong or missing key documentation, all distinct `vk` values); the conflict against the terminal's own bindings is **not** covered by any finding and cannot be settled from the tree. It is a probe, not a defect: section V's optional `InpLogEvents` edit (extended to log `lparam` on `CHARTEVENT_KEYDOWN`) and section U's **U-36B** are where it is answered. **No finding is filed.**
- **Checked — race-like state transitions: stated as a hazard class with a premise, not as a clean result.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The product has exactly two entry points that touch panel state: `OnTimer` (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2448`), inside which `PollClicks()` (`:3057`) and `Render()` (`:3024`, `:3066`, `:3092`, `:3106`) run under a 100 ms paint throttle (`:3062-3067`); and `OnChartEvent` (`:3111`), which dispatches into `g_panel.OnEvent` (`:3228`) and re-renders (`:3171`, `:3193`). The fields both paths touch are the panel's own — `m_tab` (`Ui/SSR_Panel.mqh:123`, written at `:587`, `:746`, read by every tab draw) and `m_compact` (`:97`, written at `:679`, read at `:427`, `:702`, `:735`) — and **there is no lock, latch or re-entry guard anywhere in either path**; a tree-wide grep finds no critical section, no `EventSetTimer` suppression around the pump, and no `m_in_render`-style flag. **[INFERENCE — this rests on a premise supplied to the audit, not on a line in the tree]** MQL5 runs each program on its own thread and queues chart events, so the two handlers are expected to *serialise* rather than interleave, which makes this an **ordering** question (a click processed against a half-updated frame) and not a data race. That premise has not been verified on a terminal by anyone on this audit, and the source contains nothing that would survive it being false. **No finding is filed, because none is provable from the tree** — inventing one here would be worse than the gap. The ordering question is bounded by design: `PollClicks` and `Render` are both called from `OnTimer`, in that order, so a command taken in one pump is painted in the same pump.

## E. PERFORMANCE RISKS

Scope: object writes, redraw, timer workload, tick throughput, history loading,
`CustomTicksAdd`/`CustomRatesUpdate`, snapshot cost, rewind cost, memory.

Everything in this section is either (a) a number the codebase itself records as
**measured**, (b) arithmetic derived from constants in the source, or (c) an
**unmeasured** structural cost. Each is tagged. The author has never run this on
an MT5 terminal, so no number here was reproduced during the audit.

---

### E.0 What has actually been measured

There are exactly two bodies of measurement in this project, and neither is a
clean profile of the product as it ships.

**1. One terminal run, quoted in a comment.** `MQL5/Include/SSReplay/Ui/SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38`:

```
//| because nothing had been measured slow. The user's run measured   |
//| it: 561 object properties written per STILL frame, and a mean     |
//| repaint of 39.05 ms - against an engine that pumps every 40. One  |
//| repaint was eating a whole pump interval...
//| nothing changed that is 561 writes turned into 77 lookups.        |
```

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] **What is confirmed from code is that the comment at
`SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38` says so** — not that the measurement is sound. This
section's own thesis (E.9) is that the measurement layer cannot be believed, and
it does not exempt the one measurement it inherits. **[INFERENCE, resting on that
comment]** These are the only end-to-end product numbers that exist: **561
property writes per still frame**, **39.05 ms mean repaint**, and **561 writes →
77 lookups** once the widget cache elides them. Provenance is a user's run,
recorded in prose; there is no CSV, no run id, and no way to re-derive it here.
It implies roughly **0.07 ms per `ObjectSet*`** on that machine — the only unit
cost this project has. [INFERENCE] Every per-frame write count below should be
read against that unit, not against a guess.

**[INFERENCE] One reconciliation, so two sections do not hand the reader two
baselines.** Sections M.1.2 and N.11.2 use **~586** writes for "today's frame",
not 561. The two are not in conflict and neither is wrong: 561 is the figure the
`SSR_Widgets.mqh:31-38` comment records for the repaint that motivated the cache,
and ~586 is M.1.2's **derivation** for the current rail layout — it is tagged
`[INFERENCE, from two CONFIRMED findings plus the arithmetic]` there and shows its
working. Read 561 as the inherited measurement and ~586 as the current estimate;
E.10's ranked list and N.11.2's ledger are therefore about the same frame, one
measured once and one re-derived.

**2. The 17 spikes** (`MQL5/Scripts|Services|Indicators/SSReplay/Spike/*`,
harness `Spike/SSR_SpikeKit.mqh`). These were designed to produce the product's
performance budgets — B2 `optimal_batch_size` "lock this into Feeder",
B4 `copyticksrange_week_return` "sets the page size for TickSource",
A3 `avg_rebuild_time` "feeds the Reset budget", D4 `step_back_interactive`
"whether Previous Candle is a button", D1 `bars_per_sec` "HistoryLoader chunk
size" (`docs/audit/maps/spikes-audits.md` §4). **Section E.9 shows that most of
those specific numbers are invalid as published.** No spike result CSV is present
in the repository, so not one of those budgets has a value here either way.

Everything else in this section is **unmeasured**.

---

### E.1 UI repaint is the dominant cost, and the cache that was built to fix it is defeated every frame

The panel paints at 10 fps, not at pump rate. `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3063`
gates `g_panel.Render()` on `now_ms - g_panel_paint >= 100`, and the comment at
2960-2973 explains why: at 25 fps "the two compete, the terminal goes sluggish,
and a sluggish terminal is one that answers clicks late or not at all."
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] That decision is sound and should be preserved.

What was not fixed is what each of those 10 frames costs.

**E.1.1 `DrawSheet` deletes and recreates the whole visible sheet every frame —
finding `ui-panel-1` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED).** `SSR_Panel.mqh:1270` begins with an
unconditional `HideSheets()`, whose id list (`:1301-1316`) contains the ids of
*every* sheet **including the one about to be drawn**. Counted from source:
70 named `Remove()` + 4×3 meter parts + `SSR_POS_MAX`(12)×6 row parts =
**154 `Remove()` calls per frame**, each an `ObjectDelete` plus a `Forget()`
(`SSR_Widgets.mqh:628-635`), followed by ~20-25 `ObjectCreate` and their full
property writes to rebuild what was just deleted. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]

Both caches are defeated by construction: `CSSRPanel::Text()` requires
`m_w.Exists(id)` (`:194`) and `CSSRWidgets::Same()` ends in `ObjectFind >= 0`
(`SSR_Widgets.mqh:80-88`) — and the object was deleted moments earlier. At 10 fps
that is **~1,540 `ObjectDelete` + ~1,540 `Forget()` per second** before any draw
work. [INFERENCE from the counts above]

**E.1.2 `HideBody(false)` invalidates ~44 more objects every frame — finding
`ui-panel-2` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED).** `SSR_Panel.mqh:729` runs on every
non-collapsed frame; `CSSRWidgets::Hide` writes `OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES` and then
calls `Forget(n)` **unconditionally** (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:616-626`) because
visibility is not in the fingerprint. Lines 732-734 and 750-751 then redraw
exactly those objects, so `Same()` fails for each and `Rect`/`ButtonC` execute
all nine writes (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:211-220, 377-386`). The 20-cell speed groove
alone is **22 objects × 9 writes = 198 writes per frame**; the finding's estimate
for the whole block is **~400 property writes per frame**. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE
for the mechanism and the 9-writes-per-object constant; the 400 total is
arithmetic, unmeasured]

**E.1.3 The key card is torn down and rebuilt 10×/s while it is open — finding
`ui-panel-12` (LOW, CONFIRMED).** `SSR_Panel.mqh:776` calls `m_keys.Show(m_chart)`
on every frame while the card is up; `CSSRKeyCard::Show` (`SSR_KeyCard.mqh:55-104`)
opens with `m_w.RemoveAll()` — `ObjectsDeleteAll` + `ForgetAll` — then recreates a
rectangle and ~40 labels, and `SSRKeyBindings` re-`ArrayResize`s a 22-entry table
each time (`SSR_Keys.mqh:112-122`). ≈41 deletes + 41 creates + ~450 writes per
frame, on the same thread as the pump. The *redraw* is required (creation order is
the only z-order, invariant I2); the *destructive* implementation is the cost.
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]

**E.1.4 The one uncached primitive is the one the user types into — finding
`ui-panel-11` (MEDIUM, POTENTIAL_RISK).** `CSSRWidgets::Edit` has no cache at all
and writes nine properties unconditionally (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:305-319`), while
`HideSheets` hides the tag box and `SheetTrade` re-shows it on every frame
(`SSR_Panel.mqh:1298-1299`, `:1375-1376`). Whether MetaTrader drops focus or
keystrokes when `OBJPROP_TIMEFRAMES` is toggled on a focused `OBJ_EDIT` cannot be
established from source — **POTENTIAL_RISK**, not a confirmed failure. The cost
itself (9 writes/frame + 2 visibility writes) is confirmed.

**E.1.5 A visible symptom of the same mechanism — finding `ui-panel-5` (MEDIUM,
CONFIRMED).** Slots 12 and 17 both write the object `setuprow` at the same
coordinates (`SSR_Panel.mqh:1402` and `:1432`). Because `HideSheets` deletes it
first, `Text(12)` always writes and `Text(17)` almost always takes its early
return, so `order_why` is on screen for one frame (~100 ms) and then gone. This is
not merely a paint-budget issue: it is a user-facing message that the repaint
strategy eats. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]

**E.1.6 The cache can degrade permanently — finding `ui-plumbing-6` (LOW,
CONFIRMED).** `Slot()` (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:58-77`) stops at the first free-or-matching
slot with a probe run of 8; `Forget()` (`:103`) guards on `m_ck[k] == name` and
therefore clears **nothing** when an earlier deletion in the probe chain has freed
the home slot, after which `Keep()` writes a second copy and the old one is
stranded. The panel performs exactly that Hide-then-redraw pattern 10×/s on
`stflt`/`stopen`/`stspread`/`stfid` (`SSR_Panel.mqh:1937-1940`) and on 5 tabs +
20 speed cells + 2 slider parts (`:2091-2098`). With ~200-260 distinct `SSRP_`
names in a 512-slot table, a filled 8-probe run makes `Slot()` return −1, and
every object hashing into it takes its full 6 or 9 writes forever — i.e. it decays
back toward the 561-write frame the cache exists to prevent. **Unmeasured how long
that takes.**

**E.1.7 A latent cache miss — finding `ui-plumbing-8` (IMPROVEMENT, CONFIRMED).**
`Label()`'s fingerprint folds the font to `StringLen(font)` (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:232`).
Harmless today because `SSR_FONT` and `SSR_FONT_MONO` are both `"Tahoma"`
(`SSR_Theme.mqh:424-425`); it becomes a wrong-glyph bug the day someone splits
them, which `SSR_Theme.mqh:29-31` explicitly anticipates.

**E.1.8 Stale documentation that will misdirect the next optimisation.**
`SSR_Panel.mqh:2998-3000` says "Buttons and rectangles have no cache at all, so
this [`PaintWrites()`] is the real floor of the paint." That is false as written:
`Rect` (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:195-222`) and `ButtonC` (`:358-400`) both call `Same()`
and both `Keep()`. Only `Edit` is uncached. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
[RECOMMENDATION] Correct the comment before anyone optimises against it.

### E.2 Object write accounting, as the code stands

Unit costs are exact, from `SSR_Widgets.mqh` (all [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]):

| primitive | writes when it actually draws | cached? |
|---|---|---|
| `Rect` (`:195`) | 9 (+`Common()` on create) | yes |
| `ButtonC`/`Button` (`:358`) | 9 | yes |
| `Label` (`:225`) | 6 | yes (font by length only) |
| `Edit` (`:288`) | 9 (+1 for text) | **no** |
| `Slider` | `Rect` + 20×`ButtonC` + `Rect` = 22 objects | per-part |
| `Meter` | 3 `Rect` | per-part |
| `Group` | 2 `Rect` + 1 `Label` | per-part |

Chart-side objects do **not** go through `CSSRWidgets` and have no cache at all:
`CSSRTradeLines::Level` (`SSR_TradeLines.mqh:71-95`) writes **6 properties
unconditionally** per level per call, and `Ensure` (`:100-151`) writes 6 plus a
`SELECTED` re-assert. `DrawPosition` (`:383`) calls `Level` up to three times
(entry/SL/TP) per position and performs **two `ChartGetInteger` calls per
position** (`:416-418`), and the sweep runs every 5th pump. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE;
total cost unmeasured]

`CSSRTradeLines::EndPositions` (`:445-470`) is `O(HLINE objects × positions drawn
this pass)`: it walks `ObjectsTotal(m_chart, 0, OBJ_HLINE)` backwards, does
`StringSubstr`/`StringFind`/`StringToInteger` per object, then a linear scan of
`m_seen` per object. With 30 open positions (90 `SSR_POS_*` lines) that is ~90
name parses × 30 comparisons every 200 ms. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE; unmeasured]

---

### E.3 `ChartRedraw`

38 `ChartRedraw` call sites exist across `MQL5/Include` and `MQL5/Experts`.
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The two that matter on the hot path:

* `CSSRPanel::Render()` ends in `ChartRedraw(m_chart)` (`SSR_Panel.mqh:826`) —
  10×/s, enforced by audit A20.
* `CSSRChartManager::Redraw()` (`SSR_ChartManager.mqh:531-583`) — one
  `ChartRedraw` per managed chart, plus a conditional `ChartNavigate(CHART_END)`
  only when the newest **M1** bar changed *and* `ViewOffset > 0`.

Two throttles stack and one of them is dead. `SSR_REDRAW_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 100`
(`SSR_ChartTypes.mqh:21`) is the manager's own floor, but the host only calls
`g_charts.Redraw()` on `g_slow_tick % 5` (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2828`), i.e.
every **200 ms** at the default `InpPumpMs = 40`. The 100 ms floor therefore never
fires except on `force`. [INFERENCE — arithmetic from the two constants]

**Finding `chart-2` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED): secondary-symbol charts are never
redrawn at all.** `g_charts2[i].Redraw()` appears nowhere; the host calls only
`g_charts2[i].Sync()` (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2830`). At `SSR_FIDELITY_BAR` no
tick arrives to repaint them either — the host's own comment (2825-2827) says
`Redraw` "is the only thing that moves the chart at bar fidelity." A multi-symbol
board therefore shows a still picture on every instrument but the primary. This is
a *correctness* symptom of a *performance* decision (redraw is per-instance and
only the primary instance is driven).

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE for the call sites and the cadence; the cost is explicitly unmeasured]
Also on the 200 ms cadence: `g_publisher.Publish()` for every stream,
`g_charts.Sync()`, `g_charts2[i].Sync()`, and — when blind mode is on — a
`g_blind.Apply()` loop over **every managed chart, every 200 ms**
(`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2821-2823`). The comment calls re-application free
because it is idempotent; idempotent is not free, and the cost is unmeasured.

---

### E.4 Timer workload

`EventSetMillisecondTimer(InpPumpMs)` with `InpPumpMs = 40` → **25 `OnTimer`
entries/second**. Cadences, from `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2447-2897`
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]:

| cadence | at 40 ms | work |
|---|---|---|
| every pump | 40 ms | `g_shots.Flush()`, `g_first.Tick()`, `g_group.Pump(delta)`, `RecordFlight`, `g_publisher.Poll()`, trade-line `Poll` + `NoteLineDistances` |
| `% 5` | 200 ms | `Publish()` ×streams, `Sync()`, blind re-apply per chart, `Redraw()`, trade-line position sweep + `EndPositions` |
| `% 25` playing / `% 250` paused | 1 s / 10 s | `PrintVitals()` |
| `% 50` | 2 s | `g_charts.ScanLeaks()` |
| ≥100 ms since last | 100 ms | `PollClicks()` then `Render()` |

**E.4.1 The starvation cap discards time rather than repaying it.** `delta` is
capped at `MathMax(4*InpPumpMs, 100)` = 160 ms (`:2754`), and anything above the
cap increments `g_starved` and is **dropped**. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Under UI
pressure the replay therefore silently runs slow rather than catching up — which
is the correct choice for a replay tool, but it means `g_starved` is the only
signal that the machine could not keep up. `PrintVitals` emits a LATE line when
`g_starved > 0` (`:2311`). [RECOMMENDATION] Treat a non-zero `g_starved` as the
project's standing performance alarm; nothing else in the product reports paint
cost at runtime.

**E.4.2 `InpPumpMs` has no bound — finding `host-expert-15` (LOW,
POTENTIAL_RISK).** It reaches `EventSetMillisecondTimer` raw at `:1574` and the
watchdog re-arms with the same unvalidated value at `:3149`, so a rejected
interval cannot be recovered from. Whether `EventSetMillisecondTimer(0)` is
refused or coerced to the terminal's floor is unverifiable from source; the
absence of validation is confirmed.

**E.4.3 Screenshots are taken synchronously inside the timer pass.**
`CSSRShotBook::Flush()` (`SSR_ShotBook.mqh:231-257`) is called at the top of
`OnTimer` and loops over the whole queue, taking each `ChartScreenShot` up to
1600×900 (`SSR_SHOT_W_MAX`/`H_MAX`, `:48-49`) inline. A burst — e.g. `CloseAll`
with a dozen positions — performs a dozen synchronous PNG encodes inside one
timer beat. The size bound is deliberate — the comment at `:45-47` says "a 4K
chart would write megabytes per trade" — but the *burst* is not bounded.
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE that the loop is unbounded per pass and synchronous; the
wall cost of `ChartScreenShot` is **unmeasured**.] Related:
finding `trading-analytics-15` (IMPROVEMENT, POTENTIAL_RISK) — the shots are
taken on the chart the panel is drawn on, so every PNG also contains the panel.

---

### E.5 Tick throughput, `CustomTicksAdd` and `CustomRatesUpdate`

**E.5.1 The injection rate is small — smaller than the spikes assumed.**
Arithmetic from source constants [INFERENCE, each input CONFIRMED FROM CODE]:

* `CSSRReplayClock::Advance` scales wall time by `speed_x100/100`
  (`SSR_ReplayClock.mqh:99-101`).
* Top of the speed ladder is `SSR_SPEED_MAX = 100000` = **1000×**
  (`SSR_Types.mqh:131, 298`).
* `delta` is capped at 160 ms (E.4.1), so one pump advances at most
  160 × 1000 = 160,000 replay-ms ≈ **2.67 M1 bars**.
* Default `InpTicksPerBar = 8`, floored at 4 by `SetTicksPerBar`
  (`SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:106`).

That is **≈21 synthetic ticks per pump, ≈535 ticks/s at maximum speed and default
fidelity** — against B2's own gates of `throughput_target ≥ 2000 t/s` and
`throughput_floor ≥ 500 t/s`. In other words, on the shipped speed ladder the
`CustomTicksAdd` path is not the bottleneck; the repaint path is. [INFERENCE]
This is the single most important framing correction in this section: B2's
`optimal_batch_size` ("lock this into Feeder") answers a question the shipped
engine does not ask, because the engine never offers a 50,000-tick batch.

**E.5.2 Write chunking is fixed and conservative.**
`SSR_RATES_CHUNK 10000` and `SSR_TICKS_CHUNK 4096`
(`SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:32, 37`); `WriteBars` (`:593-636`) copies each slice
element-wise into a local array before `CustomRatesUpdate`, and `AddTicks`
(`:646-697`) slices at 4096 per `CustomTicksAdd`. The comment marks 4096 as a
"safety bound, not throughput knob". [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The element-wise copy
per slice is an extra O(n) pass that a `ArrayCopy` would avoid;
[RECOMMENDATION] worth a look, but **no measurement exists** to say it matters.

**E.5.3 Per-pump emit work repeats on the forming bar — finding `core-engine-5`
(MEDIUM, CONFIRMED).** `EmitWindow` re-reads and re-synthesises the M1 bar
containing `now` on every pump (needed for `ClipBar`), and then trims the
synthesised ticks to `[lo, hi]` (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:437-460`). At 1×
(40 ms windows against 8 ticks spread over 59,999 ms) **most pumps synthesise 8
ticks and keep none**. The CPU cost is small; the consequence recorded in the
finding is that `bars_consumed` and `SpreadBarsRecorded`/`SpreadBarsFixed` are
inflated by the same factor, so the panel's "Bars" figure and the session summary
are not usable as load indicators.

**E.5.4 Performance feeds back into correctness — finding `core-engine-1` (HIGH,
CONFIRMED).** `CSSRPumpBudget` derives the per-pump ceiling from *measured*
µs/tick: `MaxTicks() = budget_ms*1000/us_per_tick` clamped to `[32, 32768]`,
`budget_ms` default 12.0, uncalibrated fallback 4096
(`SSR_PumpBudget.mqh:25-79`). `MaxBars = MaxTicks/ticks_per_bar`, so **512 bars
uncalibrated** — a cap that the shipped ladder (E.5.1, ≤2.67 bars/pump) can never
reach. But if a terminal measures 400 µs/tick, `MaxTicks` clamps to 32 and
`MaxBars(8)` becomes **4**. `EmitWindow` then *overwrites* `nb` with the cap
(`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:398-404`), which makes the later "stop short" test
`(first + bars_used) < nb` (`:524`) unreachable, so the cursor advances to `hi`
anyway — the bars above the cap are **dropped, not deferred**, and the comment at
`:519-522` describes behaviour the code does not have. A slow terminal therefore
produces a chart with holes and unevaluated SL/TP, reported to the user as
"deferred". This is the one place where a performance number silently changes what
the product does.

**E.5.5 An empty range costs 20 seconds.** `CSSRMt5SeriesGate::Ensure`
(`SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:146-180`, per `docs/audit/maps/data.md:228`) treats only
`got > 0` as success, so a range that legitimately holds zero bars (a weekend, a
holiday) burns the whole 20 s timeout and then fails, with no
`SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED` early-out. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE per the map; unmeasured in
wall time, but the timeout constant is the cost.]

---

### E.6 History loading and seeding

* `CSSRBarWindow` holds `SSR_WINDOW_BARS_DEFAULT = 20000` M1 bars in memory
  (`SSR_BarWindow.mqh:35`), with `SSR_WINDOW_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS 15000` and
  `SSR_WINDOW_RETRY_SLEEP_MS 50`. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
* **The hot read path is good and should be preserved.** `CSSRBarWindow::Read`
  (`:256-286`) does a **binary search** for the first bar at or after `from_msc`,
  then a bounded copy — `O(log n + k)`, never a terminal round trip. Coverage is
  recorded as the *requested* range, not the returned span, explicitly so a sparse
  answer does not "reload on every pump" (`:240-245`). [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
* Tick reads page with `SSR_TICK_PAGE_GUARD = 64` pages and a **separate** retry
  budget (200 retries / 15 s) so async retries cannot consume the page budget
  (`SSR_Mt5Providers.mqh:38`, map `data.md:246-249`). [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
* Warmup seeding is bulk: `SeedWarmup` does one `ReadBars` over the whole warmup
  range and one `SeedBars` (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:854-906`), timed into
  `m_metrics.RecordSeed` and fed back to the catalogue every 50 pumps
  (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2845-2849`) so the next session's cost quote comes
  from this machine. That feedback loop is the right design. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
* The seed cache (`SSR_SeedCache.mqh`) removes the warmup read entirely on a hit —
  `NeedsWarmup()` is `!m_reused_seed`, and the controller then skips the data-layer
  read (`map mt5-symbol.md §5, 106`). This is the largest *existing* win on the
  startup path. **Its size is unmeasured**, because D1 (the seed spike) publishes
  an invalid rate — see E.9.
* Caution: finding `mt5-symbol-1` (HIGH, CONFIRMED) — warmup repair after a jump
  is skipped whenever the seed was reused from cache. The performance win and that
  defect are on the same code path.

---

### E.7 Snapshot cost and rewind cost

**Snapshots are cheap, and that is confirmed.** `TakeSnapshot`
(`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1594-1603`) copies five flat structs — state, clock,
cursor, timeline, label. No file I/O, no bar read, no fingerprint. It runs when
`m_snaps.IsDue()` — first pump after Load/Reset, then every 5 replay-minutes into
a 64-entry ring (`SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:36`). [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]

The expensive sibling is **not** on that path: `FingerprintUpTo`
(`:1677-1694`) does a full `ReadBars` over `[start_msc, now]` and is called only
from session save (`:1736`) and resume verification (`:1847`). With the default
`InpReplayBars = 2000` that is a 2,000-bar read at deinit; it scales linearly with
session length. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE; wall cost unmeasured]

**Rewind is three operations, and only the middle one is bounded.**
`StepBackward` → `NearestAtOrBefore` → `RestoreSnapshot` → `sink.TruncateFrom`
→ `JumpForward(target)`:

1. `CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Truncate` (`:712-744`) — one `CustomRatesDelete` plus
   one `CustomTicksDelete`, both cutting at the same M1 open.
2. Struct restores — free.
3. `JumpForward` (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1333-1420`) — one `ReadBars` over the
   skipped span into a single array, `FilterRates`, then `SeedBars` → `WriteBars`
   in 10,000-bar slices; the partial bar is then re-emitted as ticks through
   `EmitWindow`. Back-navigation via a checkpoint replays **up to 5 replay-minutes
   of bars in bulk** (map `core-engine.md:147`).

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] So a one-candle step back is: two `Custom*Delete` calls plus
a bulk re-seed of at most 5 minutes. **How long that takes is unknown**: the spike
built to answer it (D4) is invalid — see E.9 — and A3's `avg_rebuild_time`,
labelled as feeding the Reset budget, times a flag rather than the work.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Finding `core-sync-6` (CONFIRMED, IMPROVEMENT) is the storage-side consequence:
`SnapshotStore::DropFrom` (`SSR_SnapshotStore.mqh:140-160`) leaves holes without
adjusting `m_count`/`m_head`, so after stepping back through *k* checkpoints the
next *k* checkpoints overwrite the **oldest survivors** instead of refilling the
holes — rewind depth silently drops to 64−*k* until a full wrap, while `Count()`
still reports 64.

---

### E.8 Memory

All [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] for the allocation sites; totals are [INFERENCE].

* `CSSRBarWindow`: 20,000 `MqlRates` ≈ **1.2 MB per stream** (`MqlRates` is 60
  bytes). With the primary plus `SSR_EXTRA_STREAMS` extras, ~4-5 MB of M1 cache.
* `CSSRReplayController::m_ticks` is a member array resized **upward only**
  (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:416-421`); it never shrinks for the controller's
  lifetime. At the uncalibrated cap that is 4,096 `MqlTick` ≈ 240 KB per stream.
  The synthesizer's contract (`SSR_TickSynthesizer.mqh:112-115`) is that the
  caller pre-sizes, "allocating inside a per-bar call is the kind of thing that
  quietly costs a third of the throughput budget" — respected.
* Per-pump transient allocation: `EmitWindow` `ArrayResize`s **three** local
  arrays (`seg_at`, `seg_len`, `seg_bar`) on every call — 75 resizes/second at the
  default cadence (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:424-431`). Small, but it is on the
  hot path and it is the only per-pump allocation left. [RECOMMENDATION] Promote
  to members alongside `m_ticks`; **no measurement exists** to size the gain.
* `CSSRWidgets` cache: 512 slots × (string name + long + string text) per widget
  instance, and there are nine prefixes in use (`SSRP_ SSRS_ SSRD_ SSRSD_ SSRK_
  SSRX_ SSRF_ SSRV_ SSRR2_`). Bounded and small; the risk is slot exhaustion
  (E.1.6), not bytes.
* `CSSRShotBook`: up to `SSR_SHOT_MAX = 500` PNGs at up to 1600×900 per run on
  disk (`SSR_ShotBook.mqh:43, 48-49`). Disk, not RAM, and capped with a log line.
* Calendar items are hard-bounded at 300 (`ArrayResize(m_items, 300)`, map
  `data.md:417`).
* D3 (`SSR_D3_SustainedRun.mq5`) exists to answer "does memory drift over 120
  minutes" and records `memory_stable` — **no result is present in the repo**, and
  its companion throughput gate is invalid (E.9). Memory drift is therefore
  **unmeasured**.

---

### E.9 The measurement layer itself is the biggest performance risk

Every budget this product quotes comes from a spike, and the verified findings
show most of those specific numbers cannot be trusted. This matters more than any
single hot loop: it means **an optimisation cannot currently be validated**.

| finding | severity | what it invalidates |
|---|---|---|
| `spikes-audits-5` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **A3 `avg_rebuild_time`** times `SERIES_SYNCHRONIZED`, which the kit's own comment (`SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:390-404`) records as size-independent and "a timer, not work" (~9 s regardless of 10k or 100k bars). The number explicitly labelled "feeds the Reset budget" is a flag wait. |
| `spikes-audits-6` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **D2 `worst_switch`** polls the same flag on 420 timed waits, so the "timeframe switch under 1 s" gate fails on a flag while the chart is usable in tens of ms. |
| `spikes-audits-8` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **D4 `tail_1bar.avg`** — `SSR_WaitLastBarBefore` is already satisfied before the delete propagates on **16 of 20 trials**, so the published `rebuild_over_tail_ratio` (and `step_back_interactive ≤ 500 ms`) is mostly call-return time. |
| `spikes-audits-9` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **D4's three strategies are not comparable**: `SSR_DropSymbol` closes the M5 chart at the strategy-2 restore, so strategy 1 is measured with a chart attached and strategies 2-3 without. The "with and without indicators" comparison the header promises never happens. |
| `spikes-audits-10` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **D1 `bars_per_sec`** — `MathMax(t_read, 0)` turns a readable-wait *timeout* into a *zero* wait, so the case that failed hardest publishes the best throughput, under the label "the number the user waits for". |
| `spikes-audits-11` | LOW, CONFIRMED | D1 (and A2) divide bars **requested**, not bars **accepted**; the kit's `SSR_Rate` guard is bypassed because `SSR_RateMetric` hardcodes the unit `ticks/s`. |
| `spikes-audits-13` | LOW, CONFIRMED | D1 prints its gate instead of asserting it — a run where every seed takes 60 s still reports `SPIKE PASS`. |
| `spikes-audits-12` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | B3 likewise: its only verdict is a creation failure, so 0 % tick acceptance reports `SPIKE PASS`. |
| `spikes-audits-23` | MEDIUM, CONFIRMED | **D3 `throughput_stable`** still baselines at minute 10, which the same file's comment says hides the finding — a run that fell from ~12,000 to ~780 ticks/s before minute 10 PASSES. |
| `spikes-audits-31` | LOW, POTENTIAL_RISK | **B2 `optimal_batch_size`** is chosen from aggregate rate only; the duration of a **single** `CustomTicksAdd` — the quantity `InpPumpMs` actually constrains — is never recorded, so the recommended batch may block longer than a timer beat. |
| `spikes-audits-20` | LOW, CONFIRMED | **B4 `copyticksrange_week_return`**, published as a call ceiling and as "the page size for TickSource", is a measurement of the broker's tick density over seven days. |

The structural cause is one invariant: `SSR_End` prints `SPIKE PASS` iff
`g_ssr_fail == 0`, so **a spike with no verdict at all is indistinguishable from a
spike that passed** (`SSR_SpikeKit.mqh:181-191`, map §2.2.1). [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]

Two product-side instruments are also broken:

* Findings `core-engine-9` / `core-sync-4` (LOW, CONFIRMED) —
  `RecordPump` is handed `(int)m_cursor.bar_count`, the **cumulative** counter,
  as the per-pump bar figure (`SSR_ReplayController.mqh:1035, 1110`;
  `SSR_Metrics.mqh:108`), so `SSRPerfSnapshot.bars` grows as 1+2+…+P. No UI reads
  it today, which is the only reason this is LOW.
* Finding `ui-plumbing-6` (E.1.6) means `Writes()`/`PaintWrites()` — the panel's
  own paint-budget seam — degrade silently, and `ui-panel-1` means
  `Writes() == 0` on a still frame (asserted in `SSR_T5_Ui.mq5:236` and
  `SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:5045`) **cannot hold**.

[RECOMMENDATION] Before any repaint optimisation is attempted, restore one honest
instrument: a still-frame `PaintWrites()` count and the `g_starved` counter. The
project already has both seams; it does not currently have a frame where they
tell the truth.

---

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sheet delete/recreate every frame defeats both caches; ~154 `Remove()` + full rebuild at 10 fps | MEDIUM | `ui-panel-1` CONFIRMED |
| 2 | `HideBody(false)` re-invalidates ~44 objects/frame (~400 writes, 198 of them the slider) | MEDIUM | `ui-panel-2` CONFIRMED |

| 7 | Session dialog re-parses every session file per row per render; `GetNth` is O(entries²) on restore | LOW | `ui-port-session-12` CONFIRMED, `ui-port-session-13` POTENTIAL_RISK |

| 11 | `InpPumpMs` unbounded and re-armed unvalidated by the watchdog | LOW | `host-expert-15` POTENTIAL_RISK |

### E.11 What is already right and should not be "optimised"

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] — listed so a future pass does not undo them:

* The 10 fps paint gate and the poll-before-paint ordering
  (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3057-3063` and the comments at 2960-2984).
* The widget property cache's design choice to keep text whole and compare with
  `==` rather than hash it (`SSR_Widgets.mqh:40-45`), and to end `Same()` with
  `ObjectFind` (`:80-88`).
* `CSSRBarWindow::Read`'s binary search and its requested-range coverage rule.
* `CSSRTickSynthesizer`'s caller-pre-sizes contract (`:112-115`).
* `CSSRChartManager::Redraw`'s "snap only when the newest M1 bar changed **and**
  `ViewOffset > 0`" rule (`:553-581`) — the comment records that firing on every
  new bar is what "the chart jumps" was.
* The seed cache, and `m_metrics.RecordSeed` feeding `SetMeasuredSeedRate` so the
  next session is quoted from this machine rather than from a constant.
