### S.2 The record, field by field

The table below is the whole specification of what a journalled trade is. Column 3 is the only
column that costs engine work.

| What the brief asks for | Where it is today | What must change |
|---|---|---|
| **entry** | `open_price`, `open_msc` — written | — |
| **exit** | `close_price`, `close_msc`, `reason` — written | — |
| **SL** | `sl` (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:195`) — **on the struct, not in the file** | new column, empty when `0` |
| **TP** | `tp` (`:196`) — **on the struct, not in the file** | new column, empty when `0` |
| **risk** | `risk_at_entry` (`:244`), set at `Open()` only when `sl > 0` (`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:744-746`) — **not in the file** | new column, empty when `0`; plus `risk_pct` (S.2.1) |
| **R result** | `r` column, `RMultiple()` = `(profit + swap)/risk_at_entry` (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:269-270`) — written, empty when undefined | keep; publish its basis (S.3.3) |
| **holding time** | `duration`, a formatted span from `DurationMsc()` (`SSR_Journal.mqh:86`) | keep **and** add numeric `hold_sec` — a span string cannot be sorted or averaged by the tool the CSV exists for |
| **spread** | `spread_at_entry`, `spread_at_exit` (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:221-222`), recorded at the fill (`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:747`) — **on the struct, not in the file** | two new columns, points |
| **slippage** | **nowhere per trade.** `m_exec.slippage_points` is a model constant applied in `FillPrice()` (`:120-126`) and in `StopFill()` (`:492-510`) | S.2.1 — two new struct fields |
| **setup** | `tag`, from `CSSRGroupPort::TagOrDefault()` (`SSR_GroupPort.mqh:796-797`) — written | keep |
| **session** | **nowhere.** `Bucket()` reads the hour with `TimeToStruct((datetime)(p.open_msc/1000), dt)` (`SSR_Statistics.mqh:245-247`) and buckets it, but no label exists | S.2.2 — a declared table, not a guess |
| **mistake flags** | **aggregate only.** `SSRStatistics` counts `revenge_trades`, `wide_spread_trades`, `trades_without_stop`, `ambiguous_trades`, `risk_spread_pct` (`SSR_Statistics.mqh:100-114`) — nothing says *which trade* | S.2.3 — one bitfield, computed by the one owner that already computes the counts |
| **before / after pictures** | entry + exit PNG (`CSSRShotBook`); paths are resolved at export and **not stored** | S.7 — a third kind, and the paths as columns |
| **per-trade review, later** | `note` exists, persists, exports, and has **no writer** | S.6 — `review.csv`, and a writer |

#### S.2.1 Slippage: recorded, never derived

[RECOMMENDATION] Two fields on `SSRVirtualPosition`, beside `spread_at_entry`/`spread_at_exit` and
for the same stated reason (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:212-220`: *"Recorded rather than derived, because by
the time the statement is written the minute is gone"*):

```
   double   slip_entry_points;   // adverse, points, at the fill
   double   slip_exit_points;    // adverse, points, at the final exit
```

Two write sites, both already computing the number:

* `CSSRTradingEngine::Open`, `SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:743` — `open_price = FillPrice(is_long, true)`.
  `FillPrice` (`:120-126`) adds `slip = m_exec.slippage_points * m_point`. Entry slippage is
  therefore the model constant, and recording it is what makes an **old** or **restored** file
  honest about the assumption it ran under rather than about the one currently configured.
* `CSSRTradingEngine::StopFill`, `:492-510` — and this one is genuinely new information. The
  function takes *"the worse of the level and the price that touched it"* and then applies slip, so
  a stop that gapped through fills far past its level. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] the realised distance
  `|fill − p.sl|` is computed inside this function and discarded. It is the difference between *"my
  stop was hit"* and *"my stop was hit and cost me 2.4 R"*, and it is the single most useful number
  in this section that the product currently throws away.

[RECOMMENDATION] the same two write sites also record `balance_at_entry` (the engine holds
`m_balance`, `:956`, and debits commission one line later at `:748`), which is the denominator
`risk_pct` needs. Without it, *"you risked 2.6 % on that one"* cannot be said about a trade
reviewed after the balance moved.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] All three fields are appended to the session-file record under the rule the
file already states at `SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1070-1075`:

```
                //--- APPENDED, never inserted: a reader that predates
                //--- these two fields stops at `note` and is unharmed,
                //--- and a file that predates them restores as zero
                "spread_at_entry|spread_at_exit");
```

That comment is the precedent S.5's CSV rule is copied from. It is already the product's law for one
serialised format; the journal simply has not been held to it.

#### S.2.2 Session: a declared table, not a guess

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The only clock the journal has is `open_msc` interpreted by
`TimeToStruct((datetime)(p.open_msc / 1000), dt)` (`SSR_Statistics.mqh:246`) — i.e. **server hours,
with no offset known to this program**. Nothing in the tree records a broker UTC offset.

[RECOMMENDATION] Therefore the session label may not be inferred. It is declared, in server hours,
and the declaration travels in the file:

```
   # session_table,Asia 00-07;London 07-13;NewYork 13-21;Late 21-24
   # session_basis,server
```

and `session` becomes a column computed by one function, `SSRSessionName(hour)`, fed from the same
`dt.hour` the hour bars already use. A reader that disagrees with the boundaries can recompute from
`open_time`; a reader who never sees the table cannot check the label at all. [POTENTIAL_RISK] the
boundaries are a convention, not a fact about any broker; the header line is what keeps that honest.

#### S.2.3 Mistake flags: one owner, one pass, no second formula

M.4.1's rule for `DailyRoomAfter()` applies unchanged here — *the arithmetic must not happen in the
reader*. [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `CSSRStatsEngine::ComputeFor` already evaluates every one of these
predicates per trade and then throws the per-trade answer away, keeping only the count:

| Flag | Predicate, already written | Site |
|---|---|---|
| `NOSTOP` | `!p.HasR()` → `out.trades_without_stop++` | `SSR_Statistics.mqh:458-459` |
| `AMBIG` | `p.ambiguous` → `out.ambiguous_trades++` | `:461-462` |
| `REVENGE` | `prev_was_loss && (p.open_msc − prev_close) <= SSR_REVENGE_WINDOW_MSC` | `:497-500` |
| `WIDESPRD` | `p.spread_at_entry >= 2 × out.avg_spread_points` → `out.wide_spread_trades++` | `:581` (second pass, after the average exists) |
| `OVERSIZE` | `risk_at_entry` against the session mean; `risk_sum`/`risk_sq_sum`/`risk_samples` are accumulated at `:479-485` and reduced to one aggregate `risk_spread_pct` | derived at the same site |
| `NOTARGET` | `p.tp == 0` — **not currently counted anywhere** | new, one comparison in the same loop |

[RECOMMENDATION] `ENUM_SSR_TRADE_FLAG` as a bitfield, and one new method on `CSSRStatsEngine`:

```
   //--- the per-trade answers the aggregate counters were already
   //--- computing. Same pass, same predicates, same file: a second
   //--- definition of "revenge" in the journal is how two numbers in
   //--- one document come to disagree.
   int   FlagsFor(const int index);          // O(1) against a built index
   void  ComputeFlags(int &out[]);           // filled by the pass at :406-511
```

**`WIDESPRD` and `OVERSIZE` are session-relative**, so they are not stable properties of a trade —
they change as the session goes on. That is a real property of the measure, not a defect, and the
CSV is written once at the end, where the session is complete. [RECOMMENDATION] the panel's detail
screen must therefore label them *"wide for this session"*, not *"wide"*.

### S.3 Raw versus net, and the accounting rule the file must publish

#### S.3.1 The defect

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `trading-analytics-4` (CONFIRMED, **MEDIUM**). Three readers of one account:

```
SSR_Journal.mqh:82        p.profit, p.commission, p.swap,            <- CSV: raw, three columns
SSR_Journal.mqh:394       double net = p.profit + p.swap - p.commission;   <- HTML: net
SSR_Statistics.mqh:431    double net = p.profit + p.swap - p.commission;   <- wins/losses
SSR_ClassReport.mqh:266   out.won = (pnl > 0.0);        <- from the CSV's `profit` column
```

With `InpCommission = 3` and a 1-lot trade that made +2, the statement counts a loss, the CSV says
`+2`, and the class report — the document a coach ranks a room of students with — marks it won. The
CSV header's `# net_profit` (`SSR_Journal.mqh:201`) no longer equals the sum of the column
underneath it.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The comment at `SSR_Statistics.mqh:415-430` says this was already found and
fixed once: *"Two accounting rules in one file… A statement that contradicts itself is worse than
none — it is a document the user might show someone."* It was fixed for the HTML and for
`ComputeFor`. The CSV and, through it, the class report were not part of that fix.

#### S.3.2 The fix, in the order it must be applied

[RECOMMENDATION] Three changes, and the order matters because `CSSRClassReport` reads the file.

1. **Add `net`, do not repurpose `profit`.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `CSSRClassReport::ReadOne`
   locates its columns **by name** (`SSR_ClassReport.mqh:238-245`: `open_time`, `profit`, `r`), so
   appending a column is safe and renaming one is not. `profit` keeps meaning raw realised P/L
   forever; `net` is added and is the authoritative per-trade result.
2. **Teach the class report to prefer it.** One arm beside the existing three —
   `if(c == "net") c_net = i;` — and `out.won = (Field(f, c_net >= 0 ? c_net : c_profit) > 0)`.
   A v1 file still parses, still uses `profit`, and still says so, because the schema line (S.5)
   tells the reader which it got.
3. **Publish the rule in the header, so no fourth reader can invent a fifth rule:**

```
   # result_basis,profit+swap-commission
   # r_basis,profit+swap           <- S.3.3; deliberately different, and named
```

[RECOMMENDATION] and one assertion, in `SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5`, that is the only thing that can
keep this fixed: **`# net_profit` equals the sum of the `net` column, to the cent, with commission
and swap both non-zero.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] the finding's own evidence says why it survived:
*"With the default commission 0 and swap 0 all three agree, which is why no test catches it."* A
test written at the default values cannot fail.

#### S.3.3 The second accounting split, which is not the same one

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `trading-analytics-10` (CONFIRMED, LOW): `RMultiple()` is
`(profit + swap) / risk_at_entry` (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:269-270`) — **no commission term** — while
every money measure includes it. On a scalping session `average_r` can be positive while
`expectancy` in money is negative, and the statement prints both side by side.

[RECOMMENDATION] Do not silently change `RMultiple()`. R is a ratio against risk taken, and a reader
comparing an R printed by this build against one printed by the last has no way to know the basis
moved. Instead:

* publish `# r_basis,profit+swap` now, in every file;
* add **one** column, `r_net` = `(profit + swap − commission) / risk_at_entry`, empty on the same
  condition as `r`;
* and let a later build flip `r_basis` to `profit+swap-commission` as a **declared** change, with
  `RMultiple()` as the single owner (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:269`) and `SSR_Statistics.mqh:454-457` its
  only caller of consequence.

Two columns, one header line, and the ambiguity is documented rather than argued about.

#### S.3.4 Undefined is empty, and never zero

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `trading-analytics-6` (CONFIRMED, LOW). `SSR_Statistics.mqh:526-530` leaves
`profit_factor` at `0.0` when there is no loss, on purpose:

```
      //--- profit factor is undefined without a loss; reporting it as
      //--- infinity or as the gross profit both mislead, so it stays 0
      //--- and the caller reads trades/losses to know why
```

Four printers ignore that contract and format the raw double: the KPI grid (`SSR_Journal.mqh:304`),
the by-setup table (`:359-363`), the CSV header (`:200`) and `Summary()`. A flawless session is
reported as *"Profit factor 0.00"*, which is the worst possible reading of the best possible result,
and the class report ingests the zero (`SSR_ClassReport.mqh:224`).

[RECOMMENDATION] Generalise the rule the `r` column already follows (`SSR_Journal.mqh:83-85`) into
the schema's first law:

> **A measure that is undefined is written as an empty value. Every reader treats an empty value as
> *not known*, never as zero.** Where a reader cannot represent "not known", it must print `-`.

Applied: `# profit_factor,` is written empty when `losses == 0`, and `# losses,%d` is added beside it
so the file states the reason the way the statistics comment says the caller should read it. The KPI
grid and the by-setup table print `-`, which `WriteAllMeasures` (`:1099-1103`) already does correctly
on the same page — the inconsistency is inside one document.

#### S.3.5 The units defect

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `trading-analytics-8` (CONFIRMED, LOW): `WriteAllMeasures` prints
`Average MAE`/`Average MFE` with `DoubleToString(st.avg_mae, 2)` (`SSR_Journal.mqh:1142`) while
`mae`/`mfe` are **price distances** (`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:295-299`), so a 15-pip EURUSD excursion
renders `-0.00`; and the caption compares that price distance with an average win in money.

[RECOMMENDATION] The journal is where this is fixed because it is the only surface that knows the
digits: print excursions in **points** (`/ m_point`, the engine's own unit for `spread_at_entry`),
and add money beside it where a volume exists — `RiskOf(volume, move)` is the existing converter
(`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:485-489`). The CSV gets `mae_points`/`mfe_points` appended; `mae`/`mfe` keep
their `%.5f` price meaning under the never-repurpose rule.

### S.4 The file layout under `MQL5/Files/SSReplay/journal`

#### S.4.1 What the layout is today, and why it cannot hold a journal

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Two defines and three callers:

```
SSR_Journal.mqh:23    #define SSR_JOURNAL_DIR  "SSReplay\\journal"
SSR_ShotBook.mqh:38   #define SSR_SHOT_DIR     "SSReplay\\journal\\shots"
```

| Caller | Name it passes | Site |
|---|---|---|
| host `OnDeinit` | `g_origin + "_" + yyyymmdd` | `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2169` |
| panel `stmt` → port | `"SSReplay-" + yyyymmdd-hhmm` | `SSR_GroupPort.mqh:783-788` |
| review card `stmt` | `"SSReplay-session"` — **a constant** | `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:3044` |
| `T10.8` | `"t10"` | `SSR_T10_Statistics.mq5:533` |

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Four naming conventions in one flat folder; one of them (`SSReplay-session`)
overwrites itself on every press; and `tests-b-16` (CONFIRMED, IMPROVEMENT) leaves a synthetic
three-trade `t10.csv` sitting permanently beside the user's real sessions, *"which is what any 'open
my latest journal' workflow may pick up."* Meanwhile the pictures are filed under a **different**
key — `CSSRShotBook::m_run`, a `TimeLocal()` stamp minted at `OnSessionStart` (`:196-206`) — which
appears in no export.

#### S.4.2 The layout

[RECOMMENDATION] **One folder per run, named by the run id the ShotBook already mints.** Nothing new
is invented; the existing run id is promoted from the shots subtree to the top of the journal.

```
MQL5\Files\SSReplay\journal\
   index.csv                        append-only, one row per run  (S.4.4)
   runs\
      20260913-094107\              = CSSRShotBook::Run(), verbatim
         run.ini                    identity and provenance  (S.4.3)
         trades.csv                 the v2 export - WRITTEN ONCE, never rewritten
         review.csv                 append-only, joined on ticket  (S.6)
         statement.html             the person-readable document
         trade-12.html              one-trade page, written on demand  (S.8.4)
         shots\
            t12-plan.png            before - the chart the decision was made on  (S.7)
            t12-in.png              at entry
            t12-out.png             at exit
      20260913-141822\
         ...
```

Four properties, each of which the flat layout cannot have:

1. **A run is copyable.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `RelPath` already returns a path *relative to the
   journal folder* precisely so *"the page and its pictures travel together"* (`SSR_ShotBook.mqh:36-37,
   209-214`). Under this layout it returns `"shots/" + file` — the run id leaves the path because it
   **is** the folder — and the promise finally holds: the folder is the unit a student hands in.
2. **The pictures and the numbers share one key.** No export can reference a run it did not come from.
3. **`SSReplay-session` stops colliding.** The name is derived, not passed; the three callers keep
   their verbs and lose their naming.
4. **A test cannot pollute the trader's journal.** `tests-b-16` closes by pointing tests at
   `journal\runs\test-<script>\`, and T12's existing discipline — *"T12 deletes all six of its files
   and all three of its sessions"* — becomes deleting one folder.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Nested creation is already relied upon: `CSSRShotBook::Shoot` calls
`FolderCreate(RunFolder())` (`:161`) on a three-level path with no parent creation anywhere, and has
done since the class shipped. [POTENTIAL_RISK] this depends on `FolderCreate` creating intermediate
directories, which no test in the tree asserts and the author has never observed on a terminal. The
new layout adds one level. **Add a single QA assertion for it** rather than a guard on every write.

`SSR_CLASS_DIR` (`SSReplay\class`, `SSR_ClassReport.mqh:33`) is **unchanged and stays a sibling**: a
class hand-in is a *copy* of `trades.csv` into `class\<student>.csv`, which is exactly what
`CSSRClassReport::Scan` globs for (`:296`). Keeping the two trees separate is what stops a coach's
scan from ingesting a student's own runs folder.

#### S.4.3 `run.ini` — identity, separated from result

[RECOMMENDATION] Everything `SetSession()` receives (`SSR_Journal.mqh:110-119`), plus what it
cannot ask for, written once when the run folder is created:

```
[run]
id           = 20260913-094107
build        = v125
schema       = 2
session      = friday-open
symbol       = EURUSD
window_start = 1757740800000
window_end   = 1757836800000
seed         = 41c7
session_key  = EURUSD|1757740800000|1757836800000|41c7
[execution]
commission_per_lot = 3.00
slippage_points    = 2.0
spread_source      = tick
fidelity           = REAL_TICK
[declared]
session_table = Asia 00-07;London 07-13;NewYork 13-21;Late 21-24
session_basis = server
result_basis  = profit+swap-commission
r_basis       = profit+swap
```

The `[execution]` block is the one a reviewer needs most and no file carries today: [CONFIRMED FROM
CODE] `SSRExecutionModel` (`SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:296-310`) decides every fill price in the run and is
serialised only into the *session* file (`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1060`), never into the journal. A
statement whose stops all cost 2 extra points, read a month later, cannot say why.

[RECOMMENDATION] `SessionKey()` is copied verbatim, not recomputed, and `run.ini` is written by the
**same** call that mints the run folder, so a run id can never exist without its identity.

#### S.4.4 `index.csv` — the only file that is allowed to grow

[RECOMMENDATION] One row per run, appended when the run's `trades.csv` is written:

```
run_id,ended,session,symbol,session_key,trades,net,win_rate,r_trades,flags_total,schema
```

This is what makes *"open my latest journal"* a `FileFindFirst` over one small file instead of a
scan of every run, and it is what a future JOURNAL destination lists when the user wants a **past**
session rather than this one. [FUTURE FEATURE] cross-run review is out of scope for v1 and the index
is what will make it cheap; nothing in v1 reads it except the user.

### S.5 The versioned CSV schema

#### S.5.1 The four laws

[RECOMMENDATION] Written into `SSR_Journal.mqh`'s header comment, where the honesty-column rule
already is (`:5-10`):

1. **`# SS Replay journal` stays the first line, forever.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE]
   `CSSRClassReport::ReadOne` sets `header_seen` on exactly that prefix (`SSR_ClassReport.mqh:203`)
   and refuses the file without it (`:273-277`). It is the format's magic number.
2. **`# schema,N` is the second line.** Absent ⇒ v1. A reader that does not recognise `N` reads what
   it can and says so; it does not refuse.
3. **Columns are addressed by name, appended at the end, and never renamed, reordered or
   repurposed.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] the class report already resolves by name (`:238-245`), and
   the session file already states this law for its own record
   (`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1070-1075`). This is the product's existing rule, applied to its other
   serialised format.
4. **Undefined is empty (S.3.4). A value that is zero means zero.**

#### S.5.2 v2, in full

Columns 1-18 are v1 **in v1's order, unchanged**. 19-31 are appended.

| # | column | source | empty when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ticket` | `p.ticket` | never |
| 2 | `type` | `SSROrderName(p.type)` | never |
| 3 | `tag` | `p.tag` — the setup | never (`TagOrDefault` gives `"lines"`) |
| 4 | `volume` | `p.volume_initial` via `VolumeText` (`:62-67`) | never |
| 5 | `open_time` | `SSRFormatMsc(p.open_msc)` | never |
| 6 | `open_price` | `p.open_price` | never |
| 7 | `close_time` | `SSRFormatMsc(p.close_msc)` | never |
| 8 | `close_price` | `p.close_price` | never |
| 9 | `reason` | `SSRCloseReasonName(p.reason)` | never |
| 10 | `profit` | `p.profit` — **raw, and it stays raw** | never |
| 11 | `commission` | `p.commission` | never |
| 12 | `swap` | `p.swap` | never |
| 13 | `r` | `RMultiple()`, basis in `# r_basis` | `!HasR()` |
| 14 | `duration` | `SSRFormatSpan(DurationMsc())` | never |
| 15 | `mae` | price distance, `%.5f` | never |
| 16 | `mfe` | price distance, `%.5f` | never |
| 17 | `resolution` | `ASSUMED` / `observed` | never |
| 18 | `note` | `p.note` | **always, today** — S.6 gives it a writer |
| 19 | `net` | `profit + swap − commission` | never — **the `trading-analytics-4` fix** |
| 20 | `sl` | `p.sl` | `sl == 0` |
| 21 | `tp` | `p.tp` | `tp == 0` |
| 22 | `risk` | `p.risk_at_entry`, money | `risk_at_entry == 0` |
| 23 | `risk_pct` | `risk_at_entry / balance_at_entry × 100` | either is 0 |
| 24 | `r_net` | `(profit + swap − commission)/risk_at_entry` | `!HasR()` |
| 25 | `hold_sec` | `DurationMsc()/1000` | `open_msc` or `close_msc` unset |
| 26 | `spread_in` | `p.spread_at_entry`, points | `== 0` |
| 27 | `spread_out` | `p.spread_at_exit`, points | `== 0` |
| 28 | `slip_in` | S.2.1, points | `== 0` |
| 29 | `slip_out` | S.2.1, points | `== 0` |
| 30 | `session` | `SSRSessionName(hour)`, table in the header | no table declared |
| 31 | `flags` | `NOSTOP\|REVENGE\|WIDESPRD\|OVERSIZE\|NOTARGET\|AMBIG`, `+`-joined | no flag set |
| 32 | `shot_plan` | `shots/t<n>-plan.png` or empty | no picture |
| 33 | `shot_in` | `shots/t<n>-in.png` or empty | no picture |
| 34 | `shot_out` | `shots/t<n>-out.png` or empty | no picture |
| 35 | `mae_points` | `mae / point` | never |
| 36 | `mfe_points` | `mfe / point` | never |

Thirty-six columns. [INFERENCE] A `Row()` at ~36 fields is ~200 bytes; at `SSR_MAX_POSITIONS 512`
the file is ~100 KB. The cost is one `StringFormat` per closed trade at export, once, off the tick
path — the journal is the one place in this product where width is free.

**`flags` is `+`-joined, not `|`-joined**, because `|` is the session file's pack separator
(`SSRPackAdd`) and reusing it across two formats is how a future copy-paste writes a record that
parses as two.

#### S.5.3 Header block, v2

Keep every existing `#` line (`SSR_Journal.mqh:184-216`) in its current order — the class report
reads seven of them by name — and add:

```
# schema,2
# build,v125
# run_id,20260913-094107        <- closes the S.1.2 gap: the file names its own pictures
# resumed_at,<msc or empty>     <- ui-port-session-3
# losses,3                      <- why profit_factor may be empty (S.3.4)
# result_basis,profit+swap-commission
# r_basis,profit+swap
# session_table,Asia 00-07;London 07-13;NewYork 13-21;Late 21-24
# session_basis,server
# shots,taken=41 failed=0 capped=no
```

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `# resumed_at` is not decoration. `ui-port-session-3` (CONFIRMED, **HIGH**):
`Restore` installs a saved account over streams that never rewound, so *"the trade log is rewound to
T1 while the market stands at T2"* and *"any stop or target crossed between 10:00 and 10:30 is
evaluated half an hour late, with an MAE/MFE that never happened."* A journal exported from such a
run contains excursions that did not occur. **The journal cannot fix that defect, and must not
pretend it did not happen.** One header line, and `st.Caveat()`'s existing mechanism
(`SSR_Statistics.mqh` `IsTrustworthy`/`Caveat`, printed at `SSR_Journal.mqh:213-215` and `:272-275`)
gains one more sentence.

### S.6 `review.csv` — the per-trade review, written later

#### S.6.1 Why it is a second file

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `ExportCsv` opens with `FILE_WRITE` (`SSR_Journal.mqh:173`), which truncates.
That is the same shape as `ui-port-session-2` (CONFIRMED, **MEDIUM**) — *"the moment `Create()`
succeeds the previous save no longer exists"* — and it is exactly what must not happen to a file the
user has been adding notes to for an hour. Re-exporting `trades.csv` to attach a note would put an
hour of review behind a truncating write.

[RECOMMENDATION] So: **`trades.csv` is written once and is immutable. `review.csv` is append-only
and is joined on `ticket`.** The statement joins them at render time; the CSV consumer joins them in
the spreadsheet; neither file can damage the other.

```
# SS Replay review
# schema,1
# run_id,20260913-094107
ticket,reviewed_at,rating,mistakes,text
12,2026.09.13 21:40:02,-1,EARLY+SIZE,took it before the retest and doubled the size
```

* `rating` — `-2..+2`, the five buttons of S.8.3. Empty is *not reviewed*; `0` is *reviewed, and it
  was fine*. The S.3.4 law again, and here it is the difference between a coach seeing "twelve
  trades unreviewed" and "twelve trades rated zero".
* `mistakes` — the **user's** flags, `+`-joined, deliberately a different vocabulary from column 31's
  machine flags. The machine says `NOSTOP` because it can prove it; the trainee says `EARLY` because
  only they know. Mixing them into one column would let the file assert a judgement it cannot
  support.
* `text` — free, RFC-4180 quoted (S.10).

**Append, never rewrite:** `FileOpen(path, FILE_READ|FILE_WRITE|FILE_TXT|FILE_SHARE_READ)` then
`FileSeek(h, 0, SEEK_END)`. Re-reviewing a trade appends a **second row**; the reader takes the last
row per ticket. An append cannot lose the rows before it, which a rewrite can.

#### S.6.2 The in-memory half

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `p.note` already round-trips through the session file at field 27
(`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:1097`, `:1210`) and already exports at CSV column 18
(`SSR_Journal.mqh:89`). It needs one verb:

```
   CSSRTradingEngine::SetNote(const long ticket, const string text)   // new, ~8 lines
   CSSRReplayPort::ReviewTrade(const long ticket, const string text,
                               const int rating, const string mistakes)  // new port verb
```

[RECOMMENDATION] The port verb does two things and in this order: writes the note onto the position
(so it survives a session save and reappears on resume, for free, through machinery that already
exists), then appends the row to `review.csv` (so it survives the terminal). Neither half is
sufficient alone: the session file is lost if the user never saves a session, and `review.csv` is
not reloaded into a resumed run.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The port is where this belongs, not the panel: `CSSRGroupPort::SetTradeTag`
(`SSR_GroupPort.mqh:799-812`) is the existing precedent for a typed string arriving from the panel,
including its comma-stripping — *"the statement is a CSV as well as an HTML page, and a comma in a
tag would move every column after it by one"*. Under S.10's quoting that strip is no longer needed,
but the ownership is.

### S.7 Pictures: before, at entry, at exit

#### S.7.1 A third kind, and it is nearly free

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `CSSRShotBook::Scan` (`:123-146`) queues on two transitions only. A slot that
appears in `SSR_POS_PENDING` — which `Open()` creates for every limit and stop order before any fill
(`SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:729-738`) — queues nothing.

[RECOMMENDATION] One arm, one constant:

```
   #define SSR_SHOT_PLAN  2
   ...
   if(now == SSR_POS_PENDING && was == (uchar)255)
      Queue(p.ticket, SSR_SHOT_PLAN);
```

`SSRShotFile` (`:59-60`) takes a kind instead of a bool and returns `t%d-plan|in|out.png`. The
deferral, the queue, the cap, the run folder and the rewind behaviour are all untouched — which is
the point. **For a pending order this is a true *before*:** the decision is drawn on the chart, the
fill has not happened, and the picture is taken one timer pass later on a chart that has repainted.

[INFERENCE] **For a market order there is no before, and this section will not pretend otherwise.**
The order and the fill are the same instant; a picture of the chart before it can only be taken by a
program that knew the click was coming. [FUTURE FEATURE] the honest version is a `Plan(msc)` verb
called when the planning lines are **armed** (`lines_armed` on the wire), writing `plan-<msc>.png`
and stitched to the ticket at `Open()`. It costs a PNG per armed setup including the ones never
taken, so it needs its own cap and its own input; it is not v1.

#### S.7.2 The panel in the picture

`trading-analytics-15` (POTENTIAL_RISK, IMPROVEMENT). Two candidate fixes; take the second.

* **Shoot a different chart.** `CSSRChartManager` already opens and owns charts. Correct, and it
  needs a chart that exists in every configuration, which `InpOneChart=true` does not guarantee.
* [RECOMMENDATION] **Collapse the panel for the shot, using the deferral that already exists.**
  `m_collapsed` is a real state with a 22 px frame and a `reopen` affordance
  (`SSR_Panel.mqh:641-655`). The ShotBook already waits one timer pass for a repaint; waiting **two**
  — set collapsed, let `Render()` run, shoot, restore — costs one extra 100 ms pass per shot and
  removes 310×336 of chrome from a document a student hands in. The planning lines stay in the
  picture, which is what the picture is for.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] This is affordable because the shot path is already off the hot loop:
`Flush()` runs from the host timer (`SSReplayStandalone.mq5:2731`), not from `OnTicks` — `OnTicks`
only calls `Scan()` (`SSR_ShotBook.mqh:263-264`).

[POTENTIAL_RISK] It is unverifiable from source whether `ChartScreenShot` captures objects at all on
a chart the program does not own, and whether a `Render()` between two timer passes has actually
repainted by the time the capture runs. Both are terminal questions. **The two-pass collapse is
written so that failing gives the picture that is taken today** — chrome included — rather than no
picture.

#### S.7.3 Paths in the record

[RECOMMENDATION] `RelPath` keeps its `FileIsExist` check (`:221-222`) and its stated reason — *"a
broken-image icon in a document a student hands in is worse than no column at all"* — and gains a
kind parameter. Columns 32-34 store what it returned **at export time**, so a CSV read three weeks
later names the pictures that existed when it was written, and `HasAnyShot()` (`:441-456`) keeps
deciding whether the HTML grows a Chart column at all.

### S.8 Opening one trade for review, from the panel

*This is the [FUTURE FEATURE] destination N.9 specified. Everything above ships without it. This
subsection is what it becomes when S.9's accessor exists, drawn to the constraints of M.1.*

#### S.8.1 Where it sits in the rail

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `DrawRail` needs `25n − 3` px against `SSR_SHEET_H 186`
(`SSR_Panel.mqh:1209-1225`), so `n = 7` is **172 px — it fits, with 14 px spare.** M.3.3 left exactly
this cell unspent, and N.9 named this as what it is for.

| # | id | name | conditional |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-4 | `tab0`..`tab4` | Trade, Pos, Perf, Sess, Keys | no |
| 5 | `tab5` | **Jrnl** | no |
| 6 | `tab6` | Eval | **yes** (`prop_on`) |

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The conditional destination **must stay last**: `TabCount()` is
`return (m_state.prop_on ? SSR_TAB_MAX : SSR_TAB_COUNT);` (`:1103-1104`), so the question can only
hide the final cell. Constants: `SSR_TAB_COUNT 5→6`, `SSR_TAB_MAX 6→7`, `SSR_TAB_PROP 5→6`, new
`SSR_TAB_JOURNAL 5` (`SSR_Theme.mqh:539-544`). Dispatch is untouched — the `tabN` arm tests
`StringLen == 4` (`ui-panel.md` §7.2) and `tab5`/`tab6` are both length 4.

`TabName()` (`:1106-1121`) interpolates state today, so the cell carries its own condition mark under
M.3.4 with **zero new objects**: `Jrnl` / `Jrnl %d` where `%d` is the count of closed trades not yet
reviewed. Eight characters at 44 px; `Clip()`ed at 8 under R5.

#### S.8.2 Two screens, one region, one extra teardown list

M's rule is *one swapped region* (M.3.1), and this does not break it. The list and the detail screen
are **the same region with two teardown lists**, which under R4 — *every destination owns its
teardown list, declared beside its draw function* — is one more entry in the destination register,
not a second navigator. `m_jrn_ticket` (0 = list) is the latch; a change to it is a transition under
R1, and the transition tears down exactly one list.

**Screen 1, the list.** N.9's geometry, verbatim, with one arithmetic correction:

| y | h | element |
|---|---|---|
| +0 | 13 | filter: `All` · `Wins` · `Losses` · `No stop` — four `ButtonC` |
| +16 | 15×8 | `ListRO`: time `Clip 8` · `BUY 0.42 53513` `Clip 18` · net `Clip 9` |
| +140 | 19 | pager `<` `>` + `"%d-%d of %d"` |
| +163 | 22 | `[ Save statement ]` — the existing `stmt` arm |

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE — correction to N.9] N.9 gives the filter cells as 58 px. The sheet row from
`x+8` is 237 px (M.1.3), so `bw = (237 − 3×2)/4 = 57`; four 58 px cells plus three 2 px gaps is
238 and overruns by one. **57**, leaving 3 px. One pixel, and it is the class of arithmetic that
produced four of L.3's five confirmed layout defects.

[RECOMMENDATION] The rows are `ListRO` (M.3.5) — a `Rect` well plus a cached `Label` per row — for
the list body, but the **row must be selectable**, and `ListRO` has no affordance. Resolve with a
`ListRO` body plus one 18 px `ButtonC` per row at the right edge carrying `›`: 6 writes for the row
text plus 9 for the chooser, against `List`'s 9-per-row of false affordance everywhere. The chooser
is the only clickable thing on the row, so nothing that is merely read looks pressable.

#### S.8.3 Screen 2, the detail — 245 × 186, Standard

```
  +0    18   [ < ] 38px          #12  BUY 0.42            Clip 22
  +18    1   hairline  (Rect 237 x 1, SSR_C_GROUP_EDGE)
  +21   12   setup   breakout · London                    Clip 42
  +33   12   in      09:41:07   1.35513   sp 1.8          Clip 40
  +45   12   out     10:02:11   1.35402   sp 2.1   ST     Clip 44
  +57   12   stop    1.35480    target  1.35680           Clip 40
  +69   12   risk    25.00      net  -42.10   -1.68 R     Clip 44
  +81   12   held    21m 04s    slip in 0.3  out 1.4      Clip 44
  +93   12   mae  -13.1 pt      mfe  +4.2 pt              Clip 40
  +105  12   flags   ! no target   ~ assumed              Clip 44
  +117   1   hairline
  +120  15   note    [ OBJ_EDIT  237 x 15 ]
  +137  19   [ -- ][ - ][ ok ][ + ][ ++ ]   five 45 px ButtonC
  +158  22   [ Save review ] 116     [ Trade page ] 116
  +180   6   spare
```

**180 of 186.** Row pitch 12 px is the pitch `SheetTrade` already uses inside a group
(`SSR_Panel.mqh:1407-1414`: `gy+24`, `gy+36`). Every row is `Clip()`ed under R5 against 46 characters
at `SSR_FS_BODY` — none of the worst cases above exceeds 44.

**Expanded (326 px)** spends its extra 140 px on what cannot be shown in Standard: the partial-exit
legs (`p.legs[]`, up to `SSR_MAX_TRADE_LEGS`, which exist on the struct and appear in no surface
anywhere), the three shot paths, and `balance_at_entry` / `risk_pct`. Nothing is *moved* into
Expanded — a row that only exists on a tall chart is a row a coach cannot ask a trainee to read.

**Ten new slots** for the ten drawn texts (head, setup, in, out, stop, risk, held, excursion,
flags, provenance), taken from M.7's verified free list: **72-79** and **56-57**. That leaves
7-9, 21, 58 and 59 unassigned. The `ListRO` rows cache their own; the `OBJ_EDIT` and the eight buttons
are widget-cached, not slot-cached.

**Object cost.** [INFERENCE, from M.1.2's measured primitive costs] detail screen cold:
2 `Rect` hairlines (18) + 10 `Label` (60) + 1 `Edit` (10) + 8 `ButtonC` (72) ≈ **160 writes**, ≈ 11 ms
once, on the frame the user clicks a row. Warm: ~21 `ObjectFind` and the colour writes of whatever
changed — which for a closed trade is nothing. **A closed trade does not move**, which makes this the
cheapest destination in the product to hold open.

#### S.8.4 Why there is no picture on this screen, and what replaces it

[INFERENCE] MQL5 draws a bitmap only through `OBJ_BITMAP` / `OBJ_BITMAP_LABEL`, which take `.bmp`
files or compiled resources; `ChartScreenShot` writes `.png` (`SSR_ShotBook.mqh:164`). [CONFIRMED
FROM CODE] a grep for `OBJ_BITMAP` over `MQL5/` returns **nothing** — the product has never drawn an
image. **The panel cannot show the screenshot.** There is also no way for an MQL5 program to open a
file in the user's browser without a DLL import, which this product does not have.

[RECOMMENDATION] So `[ Trade page ]` writes `runs/<run>/trade-12.html` — one page, the same
`SSRWriteReportHead` skin, the detail rows, both or three pictures full size, and the review — and
reports the path. That is precisely what `stmt` already does: [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] the panel prints
`"[panel] statement saved -> MQL5\\Files\\%s"` to the Experts log (`SSR_Panel.mqh:2616-2617`).

[RECOMMENDATION] The log is the wrong place for the *only* confirmation. Give both `stmt` and
`Trade page` the status-strip line M.3.7 already recommends splitting out — **`stmsg`, its own id
rather than borrowing slot 50 / `stbal`** — and the user is told on the panel where the file went,
in the band the status ladder reserves for things that just happened.

#### S.8.5 What the wire costs

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `SSRUiState` is flat and pointer-free, with `SSR_POS_MAX 12`
(`SSR_ReplayPort.mqh:29`) parallel arrays for open positions (`:189-210`).

[RECOMMENDATION] The JOURNAL destination adds **no second array**. It reuses the closed-rows arrays
M.4.2 introduces for the POSITIONS → Closed page — the list screen *is* that page with filters and a
pager — and adds **one gated scalar block** for the selected trade:

```
   CSSRGroupPort::WantTrade(const long ticket)     // 0 = nothing selected
   ...
   jrn_ticket, jrn_head, jrn_setup, jrn_session, jrn_in, jrn_out,
   jrn_stop, jrn_risk, jrn_held, jrn_exc, jrn_flags, jrn_note   // 12 pre-formatted strings
```

Pre-formatted at the owner, exactly as `pos_text` already is (`:190`, `"BUY 1.00 @ 53513"`), so the
panel composes nothing and computes nothing — the rule `SheetProp` states about itself
(`SSR_Panel.mqh:1732-1740`). The block is filled only while `jrn_ticket != 0`, which is the same
gating shape as `WantClosed(bool)` and the existing host-only setters (`SetTpPoints`,
`NoteLineDistances`).

### S.9 The indexed accessor, and the three findings it repairs for free

#### S.9.1 The accessor

N.9's stated prerequisite, specified:

```
   struct SSRJournalRow                       // flat; two strings, no legs
     { long ticket; int slot; long open_msc; long close_msc; double net; ... };

   bool CSSRJournal::BuildIndex(void);        // one pass, O(Total()), sorted by close_msc
   int  CSSRJournal::Count(void);             // unchanged
   bool CSSRJournal::At(const int i, SSRJournalRow &out);   // O(1)
   int  CSSRJournal::IndexOfTicket(const long ticket);      // O(log n)
```

`Line(index, digits)` (`:141-157`) is deleted with it.

**When the index is rebuilt.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE — correction to M.4.3] M states that
`m_acct.ClosedCount()` is O(1). It is not: `SSR_TradingEngine.mqh:988-994` is a loop over `m_count`
comparing a state byte. It is nevertheless the right detector, because it makes **no struct copy**,
while `At(i, p)` copies ~660 B per slot. At `SSR_MAX_POSITIONS 512` the detector is ~512 byte
comparisons and the rebuild is ~340 KB of copying. [RECOMMENDATION] poll the detector, rebuild on
change — which is the same detector and the same throttle M.4.3 gives the cached `SSRStatistics`,
and the two should share one call so the walk happens once:

```
   if(m_acct.ClosedCount() != m_closed_seen || now - m_built > 2000)
     { BuildIndex(); m_stats.Compute(m_cache); m_closed_seen = ...; }
```

[RECOMMENDATION] and make `ClosedCount()` genuinely O(1) later by maintaining a counter the way
`m_ambiguous_count` already is (`:996`) — a small change, and it must handle the rewind path that
un-closes a position, which is why it is *later* and not now.

#### S.9.2 The three findings the sort repairs

The index is **sorted by `close_msc`**, and that single property is the fix for three CONFIRMED
findings that are all one defect: *closed trades are walked in slot order, which is open order.*

| Finding | What slot order does | What the close-ordered index gives |
|---|---|---|
| `trading-analytics-3` (CONFIRMED, **MEDIUM**) — closed drawdown walks in open order (`SSR_Statistics.mqh:696-716`) | three overlapping trades A(−100, first opened, last closed), B(+1000), C(−500): the real path has a 600 drawdown, the loop reports 500 | `ClosedDrawdownFor` iterates the index instead of `At(i)`; the balance path is the one that happened |
| `trading-analytics-7` (CONFIRMED, LOW) — revenge compares with the previously **opened** trade (`:497-512`) | a textbook revenge entry one minute after a loss is missed because an unrelated winner opened in between | `prev_close`/`prev_was_loss` walk close order, which is what the printed definition (`:1196-1198`) actually says |
| `trading-analytics-3`'s tail — `win_streak`/`loss_streak` from the same loop | a streak is reported in the order trades were placed | streaks in the order they resolved, which is the order a trainee experienced them |

[RECOMMENDATION] One index, built once per change, consumed by `ComputeFor`, `ClosedDrawdownFor`,
`Bucket`, the journal's exports and the destination. **This is the best-value change in the section**
and it is a consequence of building the accessor, not an addition to it.

[POTENTIAL_RISK] `ComputeFor` currently visits slots; re-pointing it at the index changes
`win_streak`, `loss_streak`, `revenge_trades` and `max_drawdown_closed` for any session with
overlapping trades. Numbers a user has already seen will move. That is a correction, not a
regression, and it belongs in the release note beside the statement's own caveat.

---

### S.10 Text, encoding, escaping

#### S.10.1 Quoting — `trading-analytics-14` (**POTENTIAL_RISK, LOW**)

**Classification first, because the fix below is prescribed and the heading is not a verdict.**
`trading-analytics-14` is **POTENTIAL_RISK**, final severity **LOW**: the *code path* is confirmed
from source, but whether any real session name or tag ever contains a `"` — and therefore whether the
merge ever happens — is a user-behaviour question source cannot settle. Everything tagged
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] below is confirmed about the code, not about the consequence being reached.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `Csv()` (`:51-58`) replaces `,` with `;` and newlines with spaces, and handles
no quote. A tag or session name containing `"` is written verbatim; an RFC-4180 reader consumes
delimiters and line breaks until the next quote, merging rows.

[RECOMMENDATION] Replace with real quoting, which is strictly simpler than the current substitution:

```
   //--- RFC 4180. A field that contains a comma, a quote or a newline
   //--- is wrapped in quotes and its own quotes are doubled. Replacing
   //--- the comma instead - which this did - silently edited the user's
   //--- own words, and did nothing at all about the quote.
   string CsvField(const string s);
```

This also retires two workarounds: `CSSRGroupPort::SetTradeTag`'s comma strip
(`SSR_GroupPort.mqh:806-809`) and the `,`→`;` substitution that currently rewrites a session name.
**Note the sequencing cost**: [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `CSSRClassReport::ReadOne` splits on commas with
no quote awareness and rejoins free-text fields with `,` (`SSR_ClassReport.mqh:212-215`). Quoting the
journal without teaching the class report to unquote **breaks the class report on the first quoted
field**. The two changes are one change.

#### S.10.2 Encoding — `trading-analytics-13` (**POTENTIAL_RISK, LOW**), and its confirmed sibling

**Classification first.** `trading-analytics-13` is **POTENTIAL_RISK**, final severity **LOW** — the
mismatch between the file mode and the declared charset is confirmed from source, but what a terminal
actually writes for a non-ASCII name under `FILE_ANSI` is a runtime question nobody here has measured
(D's coverage statement lists "no compile on MetaEditor" among the four kinds of evidence this audit
does not have). Its sibling `strategy-integration-report-8` **is** CONFIRMED, MEDIUM, which is why the
family is worth one fix.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Both exports open `FILE_TXT|FILE_ANSI` (`:173`, `:254`) while
`SSRWriteReportHead` declares `charset=utf-8` (`SSR_ReportStyle.mqh:21`). A Persian session name
becomes `?` or Windows-1256 bytes inside a document that says it is UTF-8.
`strategy-integration-report-8` (CONFIRMED, **MEDIUM**) is the identical defect in the class report,
so this is a two-file family with one fix.

[RECOMMENDATION] Drop `FILE_ANSI` from both exports. Write the CSV with a UTF-8 BOM — the product
already reads UTF-8 as binary with BOM handling in the string catalogue (L.8), so the convention
exists; and the BOM is what makes Excel open a UTF-8 CSV correctly, which is the tool this file is
for. Keep `FILE_SHARE_READ`, which is why a user can have the file open while the session runs.

[POTENTIAL_RISK] Whether MetaTrader's `FILE_TXT` without `FILE_ANSI` emits UTF-16 rather than UTF-8
is a terminal question this audit cannot settle. **Write the CSV with `FILE_BIN` and explicit
`StringToCharArray(..., CP_UTF8)`** and the question does not arise — at the cost of writing the
CRLFs by hand, which the exporter already does explicitly at every `FileWriteString`.

#### S.10.3 Length

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The 63-character draw limit is a *panel* constraint, not a file one — the CSV
and the HTML have no width. It binds in exactly one place in this section: the twelve pre-formatted
`jrn_*` strings on the wire (S.8.5), which are drawn. Each is `Clip()`ed at its row's budget **at the
owner**, so the panel receives a string that already fits and the R5 audit A22 sees a `Clip()` at
every draw site.

| `slip_entry_points`, `slip_exit_points`, `balance_at_entry` | `SSRVirtualPosition` + `Init()` | `SSR_TradeTypes.mqh:178-264` |

independently testable. 5-7 complete the record. 8-11 give it a home and its pictures. 12-13 build

a destination added to a panel that rebuilds itself at 10 Hz makes the rebuild worse, and a rail
drawn in Compact mode puts a seventh clickable cell on the candles (`ui-panel-3`, CONFIRMED HIGH).

modal is open — gates every new clickable control, and the detail screen's `OBJ_EDIT` note box makes

leave a text field. `CSSRReviewCard::OnKey` already shows the fix.

### S.14 What this refuses, and what it does not fix

**Refuses:**

* **It will not make the journal a v1 destination.** M.3.2 rejected it on four grounds; three are
  addressed here (the accessor, the record, the note's owner) and one — `ui-port-session-2`/`-3`, both
  CONFIRMED HIGH — is not this section's to close. The destination ships when they do.
* **It will not show a picture in the panel.** MQL5 has no PNG object and this product has no DLL
  import; a button that writes a page and names it is the honest control (S.8.4).
* **It will not rename or reorder a CSV column**, ever, including `profit`, whose meaning is now
  wrong-looking and whose name is load-bearing for `CSSRClassReport::ReadOne` (`:243`).
* **It will not compute a measure in the journal that the statistics engine computes.** Mistake flags
  come from the pass that already counts them; `DailyRoomAfter`'s rule (M.4.1) applies here word for
  word.
* **It will not claim a *before* picture for a market order** (S.7.1). Pending orders get one because
  the state exists; market orders do not, and a rolling pre-capture is a [FUTURE FEATURE] with its own
  disk cost.
* **It will not put the review in `trades.csv`.** A file the user edits and a file the user exports
  are not the same file, and `FILE_WRITE` truncates.

**Does not fix, and says so:**

* `ui-port-session-3` — a resumed run can journal excursions that never happened. Declared in the
  header and in the caveat; not repaired.
* `trading-analytics-9` — the equity ring discards the half that carries the peak, so a statement's
  SVG can omit the trough its own label names. The header keeps the number; the curve is still short.
* `trading-analytics-2` and `-1` (the prop evaluation is not persisted, and resuming voids it) — the
  statement prints `m_prop.StateName()`/`Report()`/`Reason()` *at export time*
  (`SSR_Journal.mqh:286-297`), so a run that was voided on resume produces a document saying so. That
  is correct behaviour on top of a defect, and the defect is elsewhere.
* `core-engine-5` — `bars_consumed` is wrong by 10-1500×. It is not in the journal and must not be
  added to it.
* **The Persian case.** [POTENTIAL_RISK] S.10.2 makes a Persian session name survive the file; it
  does nothing about the fact that `flags`, `session` and `reason` are English tokens by design
  (they are a machine vocabulary), while the detail screen's rows are drawn text and inherit Q's
  unresolved mixed-direction problem. A `flags` cell reading `! no target  ~ assumed` beside Persian
  labels is a rendering outcome no source reading can predict.
* **Nothing here has run on MT5.** `FolderCreate` on a four-level path, `ChartScreenShot` capturing
  panel objects, `FILE_BIN` + `CP_UTF8` producing a CSV that Excel opens, and whether a `Render()`
  between two timer passes has repainted — four terminal questions, four places where this section
  chose the failure mode that degrades to today's behaviour rather than to no file at all.

## T. PRIORITY ROADMAP

This section turns the 248 verified findings and the thirteen design sections (E-S) into one
ordered plan. It adds no finding, and it invents no defect: every item below is either a
`verified.json` id, a change specified in an earlier section, or a scheduling judgement that is
labelled as one.

---

### T.0 How to read this section

**Tags.** `[CONFIRMED FROM CODE]` — read out of the v125 tree at the cited file and line, or
counted mechanically from it. `[INFERENCE]` — the fact is confirmed, the consequence drawn from it
is judgement. `[RECOMMENDATION]` — a proposal. `[FUTURE FEATURE]` — work that does not exist in the
tree at all. **Every effort figure, every regression-risk rating and every phase boundary in this
section is `[INFERENCE]` or `[RECOMMENDATION]`**, stated once here so the tables stay readable:
nothing in T has been built or measured, and the author has never run this product on a terminal.

**Severity is read from `final_severity`.** [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `verified.json` carries both
`severity` (the finder's) and `final_severity` (the verifiers'); the counts this audit publishes —
2 CRITICAL, 14 HIGH, 58 MEDIUM, 105 LOW, 18 IMPROVEMENT confirmed — are the latter. Where a finder
filed HIGH and the refuters settled MEDIUM, T schedules the MEDIUM. Two exceptions are promoted
explicitly and argued for in T.6.1; nothing is promoted silently.

**Effort scale.**

| | meaning |
|---|---|
| **S** | under a day. One file, roughly ≤ 50 lines, no contract change, no new object id, no new wire field. |
| **M** | two to five days. Two to four files, roughly ≤ 250 lines. May add a struct field, a wire field, an object id, a catalogue string. |
| **L** | a week or more of focused work. A contract changes, or a file layout changes, or the change crosses three layers, or it is ≥ 250 lines. |
| **L · multi-week** | three weeks or more, and it is dishonest to plan it as anything smaller. Every item carrying this mark is collected in T.16. |

**Regression-risk scale.** *low* — the change is arithmetic, a string, or a guard on a path that
today does nothing correct. *medium* — a shipped number moves, or a new field must be filled by
every caller, or a cache key changes. *high* — the change inverts when something happens (teardown
ordering, event ordering, epoch ordering); getting it wrong leaves an object on the user's chart
permanently, or a balance that disagrees with the trade list.

**"The specific test that proves it done"** is a column, not a paragraph, and it names a real
artefact: a section id in one of the fifteen `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/SSR_T*.mq5` scripts, a
stage in the 5,512-line `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/QA/SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5`, a spike under
`MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Spike/` or `MQL5/Services/SSReplay/Spike/`, or a numbered audit in
`tools/ssr_audit.py`. Where the proving test does not exist yet, the column says `new:` and gives
the assertion.

**One piece of bookkeeping T has to settle, because the earlier sections collide.**
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Audits A1-A21 exist in `tools/ssr_audit.py` and pass today. Six sections each
proposed "the next audit", and three of them independently claimed the number **A22**, two the
number **A23**. T assigns the numbers once, here, and every reference in this section uses this
table and no other. **[RECOMMENDATION]**

| # | Audit | Proposed in | Scheduled |
|---|---|---|---|
| A22 | No `OrderSend` / `OrderSendAsync` / `CTrade` / `PositionClose` anywhere under `MQL5/` | G.1.2 | 2.1 |
| A23 | Clip discipline: every drawn string passes a character budget at its call site | M.2 R5, M.8.1 #17 | 6.3 |
| A24 | One key list: the generated table is the only one, and `SSRKeyHint()` is generated from it | O.11 | 6.4 |
| A25 | No file under `Ui/` includes `SSR_RiskEngine.mqh` | H.8 | 2.7 |
| A26 | Every stored setting has a spec row, a `Cfg*()` accessor and a catalogue string | P.11 P11 | 6.7 |
| A27 | Digit policy: no Persian/Arabic-Indic digits in a catalogue value outside an allow list | Q.10 (as its A23) | 7.7 |
| A28 | One object, one direction: no catalogue value mixes Arabic script with a `printf` marker outside the Shape-B list | Q.10 (as its A24) | 7.7 |

**The one gate.** **[STATED PREMISE — not a source fact]** Build v125 has never been run on a
MetaTrader terminal, and MT5 cannot be installed in the build environment. Neither half is derivable

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] is the codebase saying so about itself at `SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:6-7`,
`SSR_Widgets.mqh:122-123` and `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1940-1944` (quoted in U.0), and that every
runtime claim in this audit is derived from source. **Phase 0 is therefore not a phase of work with validation attached to it — it is the
validation, with the two CRITICALs and the fourteen HIGHs attached.** No item from Phase 1 onward

### T.1 KEEP

[RECOMMENDATION] These are not "things that work". They are decisions whose violation re-creates a
defect this project has already paid for, or removes the reason it is repairable rather than
rewritable. Every roadmap item in T.6-T.14 is written to extend them. The full lists live in B.18
(layer-spanning), F.2 (engine), L.10 (UI), K.15 (data) and E.11 (performance); this is the
roadmap-facing digest, and an item here is a veto on any change that contradicts it.

#### T.1.1 Structure

| # | Invariant | Why it is load-bearing |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | `Core` includes `Common` only — never `Data`, `Mt5`, `Chart`, `Ui`, `Trading`, `Session`. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] B.1's edge matrix: `Core → Common 34`, nothing else. It is what makes the engine testable with `CSSRMemoryDataSource` + `CSSRRecordingSink`, and what would let it move into a Service untouched. |
| K2 | The five contracts stay in `Core`: `CSSRHistoryProvider`, `CSSRBarProvider`, `CSSRTickProvider`, `CSSRReplaySink`, `CSSRTickObserver`. A new data source is a new implementation, never a new dependency. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] This is why Phase 8 (import) is additive and Phase 1's `OnBulkBars` is a one-method contract change rather than a rewrite. |
| K3 | No MetaTrader API call in `Common` except in `SSR_Platform.mqh`. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] One place reads terminal facts, which is why `SSRCanBlock()` can gate every retry loop in the product. |
| K4 | `Trading → Report` is deliberate. `SSR_ReportStyle.mqh` is a leaf shared by the statement and the class report. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] "Fixing" the upward edge would put HTML in the trading layer. |
| K5 | No `OrderSend`, `OrderSendAsync`, `CTrade` or `PositionClose` anywhere. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] D's grep returns 7 hits, every one a comment asserting the absence. G.1.2 turns the discipline into audit **A22**; item 2.1 schedules it. |
| K6 | Time is `long` epoch milliseconds in every layer; `datetime` only at API and human boundaries; `Common/SSR_Time.mqh` is the only seam. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Every date arithmetic finding in this audit is a *use* error, never a representation error. That is the invariant paying for itself. |

#### T.1.2 The engine's contracts with the world

| # | Invariant | Why |
|---|---|---|
| K7 | M1 is the only base timeframe; the only two write APIs are `CustomRatesUpdate` and `CustomTicksAdd`; higher timeframes are derived, never written. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] B.15. Phase 8 must import M1 and nothing else. |
| K8 | `SYMBOL_CHART_MODE = BID`, read back — **and** `TICK_FLAG_LAST` on every synthetic tick. Both. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The belt and the braces fixed one measured failure together; neither has been shown sufficient alone. `spikes-audits-3` is that no spike *forces* it, not that the rule is wrong. |
| K9 | One wall-clock-driven clock (the group's master); streams are told an instant, never a delta; `ctrl.Pump(wall_ms)` stays out of production. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] This is why `MaxSkewMsc()` is zero by construction, and why `core-sync-1` is a gap-skip defect rather than a drift defect. |
| K10 | Integer speed arithmetic with a residue carry. No floating-point time. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] |
| K11 | The future guard has two layers — the controller clamps before asking, every provider re-checks on the way out. Do not collapse them. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `core-sync-3` (generic `NextBarOpen` raises up to four guard violations per call) is noise from the second layer working, not an argument to remove it. |
| K12 | Warmup goes in as bars, the replay stretch as ticks, truncation is deletion at one M1-aligned instant in both stores, and `TruncateFrom`'s **return** is the truth. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `mt5-symbol-6` (POTENTIAL_RISK) is a discarded return value — the invariant names the fix. |
| K13 | Zero bars is data, not failure. `CSSRBarWindow` records an empty range as covered; `ReadBars` returns 0, not −1. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] K.15. An importer that breaks this makes every weekend an error. |
| K14 | No symbol rules in the data code. Sessions from `SymbolInfoSessionQuote`, currencies from `SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE/PROFIT`, digits and point from the symbol. | [CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Phase 8 is exactly where a name-parsing shortcut is tempting and exactly where it is most expensive. |

### T.6 PHASE 0 — the terminal, then the two CRITICALs and the fourteen HIGHs

#### T.6.0 Why nothing precedes it

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Three facts, together, make Phase 0 unconditional.

1. **No line of this product has been observed running.** 31,439 lines of library code under a
   3,255-line Expert, 125 builds, 15 test scripts, 13 spikes, a 5,512-line smoke harness and 21
   static audits — all of it written, none of it run. Every "CONFIRMED" in this audit means
   *confirmed from source by adversarial review*, which is a strictly weaker claim than *observed*.
2. **The instruments that would tell you what happened are themselves defective.** 31
   `spikes-audits` findings, 32 `tests` findings and 15 `qa-smoke` findings. Six test sections
   assert facts that are false against the shipped code, so the suite is red for reasons unrelated
   to any fix. At least one audit passes vacuously. The smoke harness aborts on a condition its own
   next line repairs.
3. **Four POTENTIAL_RISK findings would change a later phase's design if they fire** — `data-2`
   (HIGH), `mt5-symbol-2`, `mt5-symbol-5`, `ui-panel-11` — and one open question (L.4.2, whether
   `CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE` reaches the panel) decides three separate Phase 6 designs.

[INFERENCE] The consequence for planning is uncomfortable and should be said plainly: **Phase 0 is
the largest phase in this roadmap and the one with the least visible output.** It ends with a product
that does what v125 was supposed to do, on one terminal, with a green suite — and no new feature.

#### T.6.1 Phase 0A — repair the instruments (before the terminal, not after)

[RECOMMENDATION] This is the one place T promotes findings above their severity, and it does so on a
single stated ground: **an instrument's defect is as severe as the worst thing it can hide.** Each
promotion below names what it hides.

| # | Item | Closes | Effort | Files | Regression risk | Proving test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

these probes cannot place a broker order, *provided* the grep is exhaustive over every path that
could reach the trade server — which is a source argument, not a runtime observation, and it is the
one inference in this report where being wrong costs the reader money. **[RECOMMENDATION] Use a demo
account. Not "anyway" — instead.** Do not run any probe in this section on an account holding real
funds, and do not treat the grep as a substitute for that.

sections independently declare it a gate on every clickable control they add — M.8.2, P.11 step 5,
R.11.2, S.13 and O all say so. Fixing it in Phase 0 costs S; not fixing it blocks Phases 2, 3, 5 and
6. `ui-port-session-2` (MEDIUM) is promoted because it is in the same function as `ui-port-session-3`
(HIGH) and touching that function twice is the more expensive plan.

#### T.6.4 Phase 0 exit gate

[RECOMMENDATION] All five must hold. **No Phase 1 item starts until they do.**

1. Compile clean; A1-A21 green, with A14, A19 and A20 each having failed once against a fixture.
2. 15 test scripts green, non-zero assertions per section, plus every new section and smoke stage
   named in T.6.3.
3. `SSR_QA_Preflight` prints GO and `SSR_QA_Smoke` completes every stage on a real terminal.
4. The 0B probe log exists, with a verdict line for each of the 30 POTENTIAL_RISK findings.
5. A one-page **measured** performance note replacing E's derived figures: per-frame property
   writes, `Render()` ms, seed rate, rewind cost, timeframe-switch cost — each with its numerator
   and denominator.

#### T.6.5 Honest cost

[INFERENCE] For one developer who knows this codebase: **0A ≈ 2 weeks** (0A.6 alone is a week — it is
thirteen scripts), **0B ≈ 1 week** of terminal time plus whatever the probes uncover, **0C ≈ 5-7
weeks** of which 0C.2 (the rewind epoch) is 2-3 weeks on its own and 0C.1 is a week. **Phase 0 is
eight to ten weeks and produces no new feature.** Any plan that budgets less than this is budgeting
for the audit to be wrong.

### T.16 The multi-week items, named honestly

[INFERENCE] Nine items in this roadmap are three weeks or more: the eight marked `L · multi-week` in the
phase tables (6.6 and 6.7 share one row below), plus 0C.1 and 0A.6, which are marked `L` but earn the
same warning on volume alone. A plan that treats any of them as a sprint task will fail. They are
collected here so nobody has to find them in a table.

| Item | Phase | Why it is multi-week |
|---|---|---|
| **The rewind epoch (0C.2 / RF1)** | 0C | A contract change (`OnRewind` gains a parameter) plus a mutation log in every observer that keeps derived state — the trading engine's balance, commission, swap, stops, trail peaks and MAE/MFE, a strategy's RNG, the market view's buffer. It closes one CRITICAL and one HIGH and it is the single highest-value change in the audit. 2-3 weeks, and the test is arithmetic on a balance, which is unforgiving. |
| **The one-window handover (0C.1)** | 0C | Five findings in one `OnInit`, including the audit's other CRITICAL, on the product's *default* configuration. The sweep, the stash, the settings adoption, the seed, the resolved window and two wrong guards. Nothing about it is parallelisable. |
| **Repairing thirteen spikes (0A.6)** | 0A | Nineteen findings across thirteen scripts, several of which need a genuinely concurrent probe (C3) or a real series rebuild (D4). It is a week minimum and it produces no product change — only the ability to believe a measurement. |
| **Challenge profiles and rules (3.6)** | 3 | Two families of pre-trade gates, a refusal surface on a 310 px rail, one test per rule asserting rule ids rather than strings, and a UI dependency (`ui-panel-5`) that must land first. |
| **The scenario library (4.5) and the filters (4.6)** | 4 | The first genuinely new subsystem in the roadmap. A file format, a picker bounded at 32 items over an unbounded file, four orthogonal filters and a difficulty projection that must not become a fifth source of truth. |
| **Behavioural measures (5.5)** | 5 | Ten measures, each needing a definition, a sample count, an absent-not-zero rule and a hand-verified run. R.1.2's contract is what makes it slow, and dropping the contract is how a training product starts claiming it can detect emotion. |
| **The four destinations (6.6) and the settings table (6.7)** | 6 | Together roughly +1,800 lines in the two largest UI files, 122 new catalogue strings, 61 settings rows, a new `panel.ini` contract and a release note about inherited settings. |
| **The mirror (7.6)** | 7 | ~200 mechanical `x` rewrites across every draw site in the panel, which must land as one change because a half-mirrored panel is a documented past failure. |
| **Import and normalization (8.5)** | 8 | A whole new provider triple that must be indistinguishable from the broker path to every engine caller, with timezone, session schedule and money properties all coming from the symbol rather than from a filename. |

[INFERENCE] **The whole roadmap, summed:** Phase 0 ≈ 8-10 weeks, 1 ≈ 3-4, 2 ≈ 4-5, 3 ≈ 4, 4 ≈ 4-5,
5 ≈ 6-8, 6 ≈ 10-12, 7 ≈ 6-8, 8 ≈ 8-10 (conditional). **Roughly 45-56 developer-weeks without Phase 8
and 53-66 with it — a year for one person either way** — and the first eight to ten of those weeks
end with a product that looks exactly like v125 and finally works the way v125 already claims to.

### T.18 The standing caveat

**[STATED PREMISE — not a source fact, see T.0's gate]** Build v125 has never run on a MetaTrader
terminal; the author has never run it; MT5 cannot be installed in the build environment.
[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Every effort figure in this section is an estimate over a source reading. Every regression-risk rating is a judgement. Every proving test named here is a
test that does not yet pass, and eleven of them are tests that do not yet exist.

[INFERENCE] **One item is known to be missing rather than declined:** `strategy-integration-report-2`
(CONFIRMED, MEDIUM) has no row, and T.17.1 says why — its fix is determined by Phase 0C's clock work
and cannot be shaped before it. Two more (`chart-1` and `host-expert-12`, both POTENTIAL_RISK,
MEDIUM) are branch points that section U decides, and one (`strategy-integration-report-9`) is
outside every phase's file set. **So the claim is not that nothing is missing.** The claim is
narrower: the most likely way the roadmap's *order* is wrong is that **Phase 0B changes the order of
everything after it.** If `data-2` fires (POTENTIAL_RISK), Phase 8's first four items move into Phase 1. If
`mt5-symbol-4` fires (POTENTIAL_RISK),
a teardown path that can close the user's own chart becomes a Phase 0C item. If L.4.2 resolves
optimistically, three Phase 6 designs get simpler and one removal (RM6) becomes a repair. If P7
measures 4 ms per frame rather than 39, Phase 6's first change stays correct and stops being urgent,
and Phase 5 should probably precede it.

[RECOMMENDATION] Which is the argument for the shape of this roadmap rather than an objection to it:
**the first phase is the one that tells you whether the other eight are in the right order.**

## U. REAL MT5 TEST PLAN

### U.0 Why this section exists, and what it is allowed to claim

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The author has never run this product on a MetaTrader 5 terminal. The
codebase says so itself, repeatedly and in its own words: `SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:6-7` — *"Eleven
releases have been shipped without a compiler or a terminal on this side, and the report coming
back has been 'it does not work'"*; `SSR_Widgets.mqh:122-123` — *"I cannot run this terminal - so
the panel measures itself instead of being trusted"*; `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:1940-1944` — *"This
project has assumed both answers about that at different times and measured neither."*

[INFERENCE] Everything downstream of that fact is the same shape of risk. Build v125 compiles;
audits A1–A21 pass (`tools/ssr_audit.py`, `audit_a1()` at :133 through `audit_a21()` at :1556);
sixteen test scripts exist under `MQL5/Scripts/SSReplay/Tests/`. **None of that touches the
runtime.** A compiler proves that names resolve. An audit proves that a pattern is absent from the
text. A headless test proves that objects compose. The failures this product has actually shipped
— a symbol that accepted every tick and built no candle, a chart handed over and never handed
back, a panel drawn ninety pixels onto the price, a timer turned back at the door forever — are
all runtime failures on a real terminal against a real broker's data, and not one of them is
reachable from the build environment.

[RECOMMENDATION] So this section is not a test suite. It is the **first contact protocol**: the
ordered list of things to put in front of a real terminal, in the order that fails fastest and
cheapest, with the exact evidence each one must produce. The ordering rule is the one the rest of
this audit uses — CRITICAL and HIGH first — with one exception stated immediately below.

#### U.0.1 The exception: three of the instruments are themselves broken

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] Before any test can clear a finding, the instruments must be able to
report. Three cannot:

| Finding | Instrument | What it does instead |
|---|---|---|
| `qa-smoke-1` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED) | `SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:396` | Aborts the entire 43-stage run on an unprimed M1 series — and the priming call is the next line. Dropped on an M5/H1/D1 chart it reports `0 passed, 1 FAILED` from a terminal on which everything works. |
| `qa-smoke-2` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED) | `SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:397` | Counts tick *acceptance* and never asks whether a bar was built. On a LAST-mode instrument it prints `OK custom ticks 100 accepted` and `VERDICT: GO` on a terminal where the replay will produce no candle at all. |
| `qa-smoke-3` (MEDIUM, POTENTIAL_RISK) | `SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:311` | Gates the whole custom-symbol round trip on `SYMBOL_DIGITS > 0`, so a zero-digit instrument skips create, write, read-back, M5 derivation, ticks, chart *and cleanup* — and still says GO. |

[RECOMMENDATION] **U-01, U-02 and U-03 are therefore tier 0 and run before everything else.** A
GO verdict from an uncorrected preflight on an index or a whole-point instrument is not evidence
of anything, and using one as the gate for the rest of this plan would repeat the exact mistake
the preflight header (`:8-11`) was written to prevent.

#### U.0.2 The bench

[RECOMMENDATION] Minimum viable bench, because the defects are *symbol-class* defects and one
broker will not show them:

| Slot | What | Why it is on the list |
|---|---|---|
| **T-FX** | Any forex pair, BID-quoted, 5 digits, e.g. EURUSD | The only class the code has been reasoned about exhaustively |
| **T-IDX** | An index CFD quoting LAST, ideally `SYMBOL_DIGITS == 0` (US30, DE40) | `mt5-symbol-2`, `mt5-symbol-3`, `qa-smoke-2`, `qa-smoke-3`, `spikes-audits-3` all live here |
| **T-FUT** | An exchange futures CFD with a session calendar (not 24/5) | `core-sync-1`, `data-4`, `core-engine-6`, `Apply247Sessions` (`SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:399-401`) |
| **T-XAU** | A metal: 2–3 digits, large contract size, tick_size ≠ point | `SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:317-322` prints the point-vs-tick-size divergence explicitly |
| **T-THIN** | Anything with real M1 holes — an exotic cross, or a CFD over a weekend edge | `data-2`, `data-4`, `core-sync-1`, `SSR_Z_Gaps.mq5` |
| **B2** | A *second broker* for T-FX | Tick-history depth, session declarations and M1 completeness are broker facts, not code facts |

[RECOMMENDATION] Terminal build ≥ 2085 for the main pass (`SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5:62-68` treats
1730–2084 as a LIMIT because `CustomTicksAdd` was still settling), and one pass on the oldest
build the audience actually runs. One screen at 100% DPI and one at 125% or 150% — every panel
coordinate in this product is a raw pixel, and `SSR_QA_FontProbe.mq5:54-57` is the only thing in
the tree that has ever thought about font scaling.

#### U.0.3 What counts as proof

[RECOMMENDATION] A test in this plan is not passed by someone saying it worked. Every test below
names its evidence, and the evidence is one of exactly four kinds:

1. **A log line**, quoted verbatim from the Experts tab, with the `[host]` / `[panel]` / `[i18n]`
   / `[symbol]` / `[vitals]` / `[spread]` prefix intact. The tree emits 100 `[host]` lines, 13
   `[panel]`, 6 `[spread]`, 5 `[news]`, 4 `[i18n]`, 3 `[shots]`, 3 `[setup]`, 2 `[vitals]`, 2
   `[symbol]`, and one each of `[ui]`, `[sink]`, `[port]`. Nearly every state transition worth
   testing already prints one.
2. **A file**: `MQL5\Files\SSReplay\qa-result.txt` (`SSR_QA_Smoke.mq5:112`), a black-box CSV
   `MQL5\Files\SSReplay-flight-<tag>-<stamp>.csv` (`SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:140`), a session file
   under `MQL5\Files\SSReplay\sessions\*.ssr` (`SSR_SessionManager.mqh:43-44`), a journal CSV, or
   a statement.
3. **A number read back out of the product**, not off a screenshot — `PaintWrites()`
   (`SSR_Panel.mqh:3041`), `FrameOverflowRight()/Bottom()` (`:3037-3038`), `StatsInto()` tick
   counts, `Bars()` on the replay symbol.
4. **A screenshot or a frame strip**, and *only* for the things that are genuinely visual: where
   something sits on screen, what a glyph looks like, whether a candle moved. `tools/ssr_frames.py`
   exists for exactly this and says so in its own header (*"The black box CSV is still the better
   instrument for anything mechanical - it carries numbers, not pixels"*).

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] The black box is the single highest-value instrument on this list and it is
**on by default** (`InpFlightRec = true`, `SSReplayStandalone.mq5:136`). Its preamble
(`SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:157-190`) already records build, terminal, terminal build, broker,
origin, replay symbol, window, window bars, `one_chart`, `reused_seed`, `picked_start`,
`start_speed`, `pump_ms` and the origin's M1 bar count — which is most of a bug report before a
single row is written. Rows are `kind=S` samples every 500 ms and `kind=E` events, flushed per
line so they survive a hang or a kill (`:104-110`). `tools/ssr_flight.py` reads one and names the
first stuck layer.

[RECOMMENDATION] **Every test in this plan runs with `InpFlightRec=true` and `InpVitals=true`, and
the CSV is part of the evidence pack whether the test passed or failed.** A passing run's recording
is the baseline that makes the next failing one readable.

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] One known defect in that instrument: `chart-13` (LOW, CONFIRMED) — the
recorder truncates `chart_id` to 32 bits at `SSR_FlightRecorder.mqh:256`, so the column that says
*which chart* a fault happened on is corrupt. Read the `chart_sym` column instead until it is
fixed.

#### U.0.4 Hygiene between runs

[CONFIRMED FROM CODE] `SSR_Z_Cleanup.mq5` removes spike symbols, their charts, global variables
and result files, and the engine itself prints its name when a replay symbol will not delete
(`SSR_Z_Cleanup.mq5:22-25`). `SSR_Z_Gaps.mq5` answers the one question that otherwise costs a
round trip — *the clock advanced and no candle appeared: was there nothing to emit, or did the
engine emit nothing?* — in about a second.

[RECOMMENDATION] Between tiers: run `SSR_Z_Cleanup`, confirm Market Watch holds no `*.SSR*`
symbol, and confirm `MQL5\Files\SSReplay\sessions\` holds only sessions you meant to keep. A
leftover replay symbol is not a neutral condition — it is precisely the input that puts the
product down the `Adopt()` path (`mt5-symbol-2`, `mt5-symbol-3`) instead of the `Create()` path,
and a run that accidentally takes that path will produce results attributed to the wrong code.

## TIER 0 — MAKE THE INSTRUMENTS TELL THE TRUTH

### U-01 — Preflight must be able to fail on a LAST-mode instrument
**Clears:** `qa-smoke-2` (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED) · **Depends on:** nothing
**Bench:** T-IDX, T-FUT

[RECOMMENDATION] The preflight is the gate for this entire plan, and on the symbol class where
this product's longest-lived defect lives, it cannot fail. Fix it first, then use it.

1. Patch `SSR_QA_Preflight.mq5` section 4 so that after `CustomSymbolCreate` succeeds it does what
   `CSSRCustomSymbolManager::Create` does at `SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:383-395`: force
   `SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID`, read the property back, and report a BLOCKER if it did not take.
2. Patch the tick block at `:387-402` to set `TICK_FLAG_LAST` alongside `TICK_FLAG_BID|TICK_FLAG_ASK`
   (as the engine's own comment at `SSR_CustomSymbolManager.mqh:380-381` says the shipped ticks do).
3. After `CustomTicksAdd` returns, read `SeriesInfoInteger(test, PERIOD_M1, SERIES_BARS_COUNT)`
   and `SeriesInfoInteger(test, PERIOD_M1, SERIES_LASTBAR_DATE)` and assert the bar count grew or
   the last bar moved. Report `Blocker` if it did not.
4. Run the patched preflight on T-IDX. Run it again on T-FX.

**Expected:** T-FX prints `OK` for the new *bar was built* check. T-IDX prints either `OK` (the
chart-mode force worked and bars build) or a `BLOCKER` naming the chart mode — **never** a bare
`OK custom ticks 100 accepted` followed by `GO`.

**Proof:** the Experts tab. A new line of the form
`  OK       custom ticks built a bar               ...` or
`  BLOCKER  custom symbol chart mode               reads <n>, not BID`, and the summary count in
the verdict block.

**Clears/confirms:** clears `qa-smoke-2`. If step 3 fails on T-IDX *after* step 1 forced BID, that
is a new and much larger finding and the run stops here — it would mean
`SYMBOL_CHART_MODE_BID` does not take on this terminal, which is the assumption the whole
custom-symbol transport rests on.
